items.statement: Aim to reach 2 million tons LPG distribution volume in coming years, targeting 50% growth rate
items.quote: We have always had aim to reach 2 million tons in distribution in coming times ahead.

items.statement: JNPA Port: executing ~318,100 cbm liquid, 77,236 MT LPG, bottling plant 35k MT/yr at ~INR1,675 crore; Phase 1 (100k cbm) Q3 FY27
items.quote: executing a major expansion of approximately 318,100 cubic meters of additional liquid storage, 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity and an LPG bottling plant with 35,000 metric tons of annual capacity with a total capital outlay of roughly INR1,675 crores

items.statement: JNPA Board approved 52,000 MT refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank
items.quote: the Board of Directors in its recent meeting has approved the development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank at JNPA

items.statement: Targeting gearing ratio ~0.6; funding $5B capex via balanced mix of equity, internal accruals, debt; Aegis Vopak self-funded via equity dilution
items.quote: We'll pursue this growth with disciplined funding through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6

items.statement: CPG division targets quarterly breakeven in 4-5 quarters via margin-accretive model
items.quote: In terms of a quarterly breakeven for this business, we are working towards another 4 or 5 quarters. We should have a quarterly breakeven on this business.

items.statement: Nutra EBITDA margin steady state expected at 12-15% once scale normalizes
items.quote: From an EBITDA margin perspective, steady state is likely between 12% and 15%.

items.statement: Jaggery plant in Karnataka to commission in 6 months, will more than double capacity
items.quote: The plant will be commissioned in 6 months' time. It is coming up in Karnataka. It will more than double our current jaggery capacity.

items.statement: Jaggery turnover from both plants expected near Rs 100 crore once fully running
items.quote: Once we have both plants running, we should be able to do closer to Rs. 100 crores in terms of turnover, just from both of these plants.

items.statement: Sugar prices moved above Rs 45-46/kg; may correct once crushing starts
items.quote: In the current month, sugar prices have moved well north of Rs. 45-Rs.46 per kg. We will need to wait and see if these hold. Perhaps once crushing starts, it is very likely that there may be some correction.

items.statement: TN/AP cane availability declining; expect flat to 5% drop in crush this season
items.quote: In the current year, yes, probably there is going to be a flat or about a 5% drop in these geographies.

items.statement: Employee cost rose due to VSS at legacy plants; more VSS planned to reduce fixed costs
items.quote: They have gone up because of VSS which we have done. A lot of our legacy plants we are offering VSS. You will see more of that. This is being done with a longer term interest in mind. And overall bringing the fixed cost position down.

items.statement: Ethanol-sugar mix optimized dynamically; 582 KLPD ethanol capacity (120 KLPD grain); OMC commitments limit switching
items.quote: 582 KLPD is our capacity, which is roughly about Rs. 18 crore liters, out of which about 120 KLPD is our grain capacity. In terms of switching between ethanol and sugar that is an evaluated call we have to take depending on the margin profit.

items.statement: CPG shift to value-added products (jaggery, brown sugar) and distribution expansion driving margin pool growth despite revenue decline
items.quote: Yes, value mix shifting more towards value-added. I think you have seen that shift play out in Quarter 1. We will see more of that play out. I think adding new products, jaggery, brown sugar, etc., is a big area of focus.

items.statement: JLR targets 10% revenue growth per annum with significant focus on US market
items.quote: So we are setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum and focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.

items.statement: JLR aims to save $1.7 billion on ex-works cost, warranty, and fixed cost base
items.quote: On costs, our focus is the ex-works cost of our cars, warranty, and our fixed cost base. And our intent is to save $1.7 billion in this space.

items.statement: TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27, maintaining ~2x industry growth pace
items.quote: We would like to keep that kind of momentum going forward. So, I would definitely be targeting higher double-digit growths in FY 27.

items.statement: TMPV capex at Rs 1,300 Cr in Q1; will step up for next growth phase per Investor Day guidance
items.quote: Our Capex at Rs. 1,300 Cr for the quarter, this is still tracking last year's trends, but we will see it step-up as we execute our next phase of growth in line with our Investor Day guidance.

items.statement: JLR Q1 EBIT margin 2.8%; VME rose to 7.1% driven by China luxury taxes and US market normalization
items.quote: VME in the second big column is significantly higher. It's now at 7.1%. China is the most difficult market year-over-year for us given economic and retailer stress and also the effect of the new luxury taxes that came into force after Q1 last year.

items.statement: TMPV took cumulative 1% price increase (0.5% each in April and July); will take further calibrated increases through year
items.quote: We have already taken a 1% cumulative price increase across April and July and while we will be taking calibrated increases through the rest of the year...

items.statement: TMPV accelerating cost reduction initiatives; achieved 1.5% benefit in Q1, expecting incremental gains in Q2
items.quote: We are also having strong cost reduction programs that we are accelerating. We had a 2% benefit YoY. In Q1 itself, we had 1.5%. We'll get incrementally more this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue growth momentum expected to continue for 3-4 quarters; freight rates rising is positive for freight forwarding
items.quote: I would not put any number, but this growth momentum would continue for coming quarters, three to four quarters, which we have seen in first quarter also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 275 bps YoY to 9.34% in Q1 FY27; further improvement expected from technology and cost rationalization
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.

items.statement: Warehousing gross margin is 15-20%; contribution expected to grow from 15% to 17-18% by year-end and ~20% eventually
items.quote: But on absolute margin if you talk about it is 15 % to 16% gross margin at which we operate in the warehousing business, 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Volume growth 6-7% YoY in Q1; rest of 18.4% revenue growth from freight rate increases due to geopolitical volatility
items.quote: If you see the number of shipment, the shipment growth is around 6% to 7% as compared to last year. And rest of the growth has been happen from the freight rates.

items.statement: Asset-light model to continue; investments primarily in technology (AI-based application launched July 1) and selective leased warehousing
items.quote: Whatever the investment will happen will happen primarily means as of now it's primarily focusing on asset-light model only.

items.statement: Ocean export freight rates rising; air freight benefiting from cargo shifting from ocean; this incremental profitability expected to continue 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Incremental profitability in our industry is in ocean exports, if the ocean exports right now going up because the freight rates are going up.

items.statement: Freight rate growth sustainability may not be long-term; volume growth essential for India's export economy
items.quote: The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term. So our growth has been a mix of 6 %, 7% growth in the volume growth and another growth is the freight rate growth.

items.statement: DSO improved from 72 days to 56-57 days; working capital discipline supporting operating profitability
items.quote: At one point of time our DSO or collection cycle increased to almost 72 days, which has come down now to 57 day, 56 days.

items.statement: AI-based application launched July 1 automating 42,000 annual shipments; reducing paperwork, TAT, and manpower costs
items.quote: We have almost we have done 40,000 shipments last year, 42,000 shipments. So we created 42,000 files manually. Now we are basically automating this entire process.

items.statement: Targeting 20% revenue growth for FY27; Q1 achieved 18% growth
items.quote: So the 20%, as I said, that is definitely what we are working towards. And Q1 has been at 18% growth, as far as revenue is concerned.

items.statement: Engineering capex ~INR400 crores for stamping capacity in Gujarat, Gurgaon, Bangalore; land acquired in Gujarat
items.quote: We are investing in Stamping capacity enhancement in Gujarat, in Gurgaon and in Bangalore. So in these 3 places, we -- as you might be knowing, we have acquired land in Gujarat for EV project and Stamping project.

items.statement: Full-year capex for Engineering division guided at INR110 crores
items.quote: The capex is about INR110 crores.

items.statement: Engineering division has LOI from Tata for ~INR150 crores battery project; project on hold pending Tata Group decision
items.quote: We had bagged LOI from Tata, which is about INR150-odd crores. But you might have seen that yesterday, in the newspaper, news related to Tata, Agratas and others, there are issues.

items.statement: Home Appliances PBDIT margin target: early double digits (10%+); Q1 FY27 PBDIT margin 5.79% vs 5.34% YoY
items.quote: So PBDIT should be early double digit in my opinion.

items.statement: Gross margin down ~160 bps YoY due to commodity/forex; cost initiatives offsetting at PBDIT level
items.quote: Our gross margin is down by about 160 basis points because of the material cost increase.

items.statement: AC volume growth 6-8% YoY in Q1 (industry ~20%+); disadvantaged by new energy ratings making products 10-15% costlier; focusing on higher-capacity models
items.quote: The new rating, as you might realize, is about 10% to 15% more expensive than the market. And therefore, we did not have the advantage of the older-rated products with a price advantage in the market.

items.statement: Targeting 50-60% AUM growth for FY27
items.quote: We have committed, that 50 % to 60% of AUM growth at the start of this financial year, we'll continue to, we are continuing to pursue that.

items.statement: Targeting debt-to-equity of 4-4.5x for FY27 with 15-20% co-lending share
items.quote: Our targeted range is about where the industry is right now, which is at 4x and beyond that, we will also have participation in terms of co -lending. Our idea of having a co -lending proportion of at least 15% to 20% by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Investing in compliance software and team for middle-layer NBFC and RBI regulations
items.quote: We got head of compliance as well as a whole team under the compliance set, as well as we are investing in software to ensure that we are fully compliant for both, middle layer regulation as well as new RBI compliance regulations.

items.statement: Yields stable at 20%, targeting 20-20.5%; cost of funds to decline with rating upgrade and co-lending; opex/AUM to fall with scale
items.quote: The yields have been stable at 20%. These yields will not go down, they trying to increase these yields. You can assume that it will it will stabilize somewhere around 20% or 20.5%.

items.statement: Targeting steady-state ROA of 3-3.5% and ROE of 18% over medium term
items.quote: If you ask us ROA, ROE guidance for the next five years, we ideally would want to be at a 3 %, 3.5% ROA and a 18% ROE kind of a number. That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Gold price correction reduces ticket sizes and industry growth; new branch expansion offsets impact for small NBFC
items.quote: If you look at historically, whenever the gold prices are corrected or subdued, the gold loan industry did not grow to that extent. It has an industry-wide direct correlation.

items.statement: Implemented RBI-mandated segregation of consumption loans (tiered LTV 75-85%) and income-generating loans (board-approved policy)
items.quote: In terms of LTV, that is where the major changes have happened, wherein RBI wanted to segregate clearly between consumption loan and income generating loan. That we have implemented.

items.statement: Gross NPA 0.54%, Net NPA 0.48%; conservative LTV and collateral management protect portfolio despite gold price volatility
items.quote: Our NPAs have been pretty much stable, pretty much under control. It is at 0.54% gross NPA and 0.48% net NPA.

items.statement: Branch network grew 42% YoY to 118; target avg AUM/branch Rs 12-13 cr; new branch breakeven at Rs 5-6 cr in 12-18 months
items.quote: Our branch network has increased from 83 count to 118 branches as of 30th June, which is a 42% increase.

items.statement: Expanding organically to adjacent states (e.g., Odisha) after saturating current four southern states
items.quote: We will continue to do that and then we will cater to adjacent states. Just to give an example, we are already there till Visakhapatnam border. The next best location is Orissa.

items.statement: Capital sufficient for FY27 growth: Rs 350 cr net worth + Rs 100 cr cash + co-lending + Rs 30 cr promoter warrants can support AUM to Rs 1,900-2,000 cr
items.quote: On a Rs. 1,270 crores, we are almost adding Rs. 700 crores which will again take us to Rs. 1,900 crores to Rs. 2000 crores kind of an AUM.

items.statement: Current cost of borrowing 11-11.5%, opex 6-7%; spread 100-200 bps pre-tax; NIM expansion from yield increase, cost decline, opex leverage
items.quote: Our average cost of funds or cost of borrowing to say is about 11 % to 11.5%, that's the range with an opex cost of about average 6% to 7%.

items.statement: No major regulatory changes expected for gold loans in next 12-24 months; RBI framework already implemented
items.quote: I think whatever they had to give, they have given already.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 thermal plant full commissioning delayed to Q2 FY28 (June-July 2027) due to logistical delays from global conflict
items.quote: So, what that has done is it has moved the commissioning by a couple of months to probably Q2 of FY27-28. We are looking around the June-July timeframe.

items.statement: 100 MW solar plant to be commissioned by end of September 2026
items.quote: Solar plant is set to be commissioned by the end of September.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 project cost INR400 million (INR300 million debt, INR100 million equity), no change in debt profile
items.quote: The project cost is INR400 million, out of which INR300 million is debt and INR100 is equity. So, that remains constant.

items.statement: Zambia energy sustainable EBITDA margin 45-50% at consolidated level
items.quote: Around like 45% to 50% is the EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 35-40% after intersegment eliminations
items.quote: And when it comes to consolidated EBITDA, it will be between 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Metals business margins expected stable to slightly higher, no downward trend seen through FY27
items.quote: We could probably either see stability in terms of where we are today or if not, a slight increase. But I don't see a downward trend, at least until the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Actively investigating renewable opportunities (solar, wind, battery storage) in India and internationally; monitoring SMR nuclear technology
items.quote: We, as a company, are looking seriously at the renewable space, and not just solar. We're looking at solar. We're looking at wind. We're looking with a combination of both of them with battery storage.

items.statement: Nava Limited owns 100% of Nava Global (ultimate owner of Zambia assets); no spin-off/IPO plans disclosed
items.quote: The ultimate owner, yes, is Nava because it owns 100% of Nava Global.

items.statement: Revenue target raised to over INR3,200 crores for FY27, with confidence to surpass INR3,250 crores
items.quote: We are confident we will be surpassing this and we will be achieving a revenue more than INR3,200 crores in FY 2027.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue trajectory: Q2 ~INR840 crores, Q3 ~INR850 crores, Q4 ~INR900 crores
items.quote: We'll be crossing INR840 crores for Q2. And the total comes to about INR3,250 crores plus. And Q3, we'll be crossing INR850 crores and then Q4 is about INR900 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 4.6% in Q1 FY27; expect progressive improvement from Q3 as air freight ceases and price settlements realized
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR34.8 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 4.6%.

items.statement: Target full-year EBITDA margin of 12% for FY27, confident of achieving despite near-term pressures
items.quote: Our target -- we had mentioned last year that we -- our target should be around 12%. We will be achieving the 12% target.

items.statement: Raw material settlement lag impacted Q1 by ~INR10 crores; aluminum prices up 57% YoY (INR222 to INR349/kg)
items.quote: The settlement lag resulted in an estimated impact of approximately INR10 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: One customer agreed to pay ~50% of air freight costs incurred; negotiations ongoing with others
items.quote: And in fact, one of the customers has agreed to pay us a freight and which would be accounted for as and when we get it. And that's almost 50% of whatever will be already incurred.

items.statement: Capex focused on completing 54 launch programs; minimal new investments for 1 year, then stabilize before larger projects
items.quote: We are making investments there, but we are also curbing the investments. And -- but having said that, after this, I think for 1 year, we are going to invest only wherever absolutely necessary.

items.statement: 55 new programs in launch phase (28 launched, in ramp-up); long-term programs for Toyota, Ford, BMW with 7-8 year life, single-source, highly profitable
items.quote: There are around 55 new programs in launch phase, out of which 28 programs already launched and are in ramp-up phase. These are long-term programs for Toyota, Ford and BMW with program life of more than 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: July revenue ~INR300 crores, indicating strong demand momentum continuing into Q2
items.quote: Like I mentioned that in the month of July, we have done almost INR300 crores, and we are heading for plus...

items.statement: Shipping route disruptions increased ocean freight transit from 5 to 9 weeks, causing air freight dependency; geopolitical risk (Iran/West Asia) could prolong
items.quote: disruption in global shipping routes due to increase in ocean freight transit time from 5 weeks to 9 weeks, which led to greater resilience on the air shipments to maintain supply continuity.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20% YoY, driven mainly by exports as domestic facility ramps up
items.quote: So right now for the current year, our target is to have a growth of around 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: By 2030, domestic business expected to reach ~50% of total revenue, implying ~INR550-600 cr total revenue
items.quote: As I said on by 2030, we are expecting 50% of our revenue to be domestic. At current rate we are at around INR280 crores in exports. So a rough calculation you can make based on this that it would be around, you know, INR550 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: Five-year vision: revenue more than double current levels
items.quote: And in five years down the line, we look forward for a revenue which would be more than double of what it is right now.

items.statement: New Andheri facility: 5,360 sq ft, 125-150 kg/year capacity, adds 50-60% to overall capacity
items.quote: The facility covers approximately 5,360 square feet and has an estimated manufacturing capacity of around 125 kg to 150 kg of jewellery per annum. This is expected to increase our overall manufacturing capacity by approximately 50% to 60%.

items.statement: New facility revenue potential INR250-300 cr at peak capacity; FY27 contribution only INR15-20 cr as samples/pitching phase
items.quote: So we expect all this put together, it should be around a INR250 crores to INR300 crores kind of a revenue generation capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 10.14% from 7.35%; export margins sustainable, domestic margins initially tighter but expected to converge over time
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 7.35% to 10.14%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond jewellery <5-7% of revenue currently; major push planned in domestic B2C and US exports
items.quote: Right now our lab -grown jewelry percentage is maybe less than 5%, 7% because most of our business in Middle East which is not, you know, too much active into lab-grown yet.

items.statement: Domestic India market prioritized over new export markets due to geopolitical stability and consumption traction
items.quote: Right now, seeing at the geopolitical situation, like a couple of years, we are hopeful that we will spend more strength on the Indian domestic market, which is actually doing better than most of the other countries.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of convertible warrants raised ~INR27 cr for facility expansion, working capital, strategic initiatives
items.quote: So that would predominantly suffice our expansion in the domestic market in terms of working capital, which is around what we are raising is around INR27 crores.

items.statement: Hormuz/logistics disruption in Feb-Mar 2026 caused ~1 month shipping halt; minimal business impact as Q1 revenue grew YoY
items.quote: Only in the first 15, 20 days like I think from end of February to around third week of March there was a issue because all the commercial air flight operations and all were stopped. So, shipping jewelry was not happening for a month or so. After that the business, from the business aspect, things were normal.

items.statement: Gold hedging: natural hedge via import/export at same price; Diamonds: forward contracts hedging receivables 4-6 months out
items.quote: For gold there is a natural hedge because we import and export the gold at predominantly the same price. For diamonds we have a forward contract policy where we based on our receivables planning, we do a hedging of the receivables for four to six months.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 60-65% of revenue; 500+ commercial designs produced monthly
items.quote: Top 10 customers would be, one second I'll just have a look. Maybe around 60% to 65%.

items.statement: B2C retail launch targeted around Diwali 2026 (current calendar year); initially insignificant revenue but expected to become significant contributor over time
items.quote: Anytime in the current year we are we are definitely, current calendar year. So we are looking at say around Diwali time or something, we should be launching something in B2C.

items.statement: US export share dropped from 20-30% to <10% due to tariff issues; now stabilizing and showing better growth in lab-grown
items.quote: Currently it is, so till about a year before it used to be around 20 % to 30%. Now it has dropped right now below 10%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of Rs 800 crores maintained; on track to achieve it
items.quote: For FY27, we are on track with, you know, whatever we have targeted in terms of the top line. And we don't anticipate any problem in achieving that.

items.statement: Annual outlook unchanged; expect to operate existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization
items.quote: Our annual outlook remains unchanged for FY27, and we expect to operate our existing 7,500 MVA capacity at almost full utilization.

items.statement: Phase-3 expansion adding 6,500 MVA capacity on track for commissioning in April 2027; civil work done, equipment ordered
items.quote: Our CAPEX project, our expansion Phase-3, which will add about 6,500 MVA capacity, remains on track for commissioning in April 2027.

items.statement: Order book stands at nearly Rs 500 crores as of today, split 70% domestic and 30% export
items.quote: We have an order book of almost very close to 500 crores as of today. This is over and above whatever we have already shipped out till yesterday.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline: mostly Q2, Q3 and some Q4; fully booked for Q2
items.quote: These orders are mostly for Q2, Q3 and some of them are for Q4 also. And as I said earlier, we are expecting more orders which will be again for Q3 and Q4. We are fully booked for Q2.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margins impacted by lower export mix and partial pass-through of higher raw material prices; expect improvement in Q2 onwards
items.quote: Profitability margins for the quarter reflect both. A lower export mix and partial pass-through of higher raw material prices.

items.statement: Passed on 50-60% of raw material price increase to customers for Q1 orders; current orders at market prices
items.quote: We could pass on, you know, probably I would say about 50 -60% of the price rise to the customer. But whatever we are executing now is all at the current market price.

items.statement: Domestic vs export EBITDA margin difference is about 10%; current order book at current raw material prices with reasonable margins
items.quote: I would say the difference is about 10%.

items.statement: Expect higher EBITDA in Q2 onwards compared to Q1
items.quote: Yes, it will be higher. I mean, we hope to achieve more EBITDA.

items.statement: Underlying customer demand in Middle East and North America remains firm; customers lifting bare minimum volumes due to high shipping costs
items.quote: Underlying customer demand in both regions remains firm, but customers are currently lifting the bare minimum volume they need.

items.statement: Domestic market demand strong; no pressure on domestic transformer prices
items.quote: Domestic market is, you know, is normal what it used to be, you know, about two years back and last year. And same thing is happening right now also. There is no change.

items.statement: Container shipping costs risen 3-5x for certain geographies vs pre-crisis levels; not a demand issue but cost/logistic issue
items.quote: Container costs have risen between three to five times for certain geographies as compared to levels before the crisis.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in West Asia persists; if unchanged, exports may continue to see impact from elevated shipping costs
items.quote: While exports may continue to see some impact from elevated shipping costs if the situation in West Asia remains unchanged.

items.statement: New 220kV transformer production to start April 2027; initial margins lower to create references and penetrate market
items.quote: Initially, being new in the market, our margins will be lower mainly to create references and to penetrate into the market.

items.statement: FY27 capex budgeted at INR 9,064 crores; similar level projected for FY28
items.quote: FY27, the capex numbers are INR9,064 crores we have budgeted, projected. And similar kind of numbers should be for FY28 as well.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin boosted by INR 193 cr inventory gain and INR 301 cr trading gain; sustainable if spot-long-term price gap persists
items.quote: Inventory gains are at INR193 crores and trading gains are at INR301 crores. So that's exactly because of the higher margin and also higher inventory valuation.

items.statement: Indian gas demand supported by government allocation; replacement volumes covering >2/3 of missing Qatar cargoes via tolling contracts
items.quote: whatever we are missing from the Middle East, actually more than two-third is being brought by these customers. So, we hope that this will this trend will continue.

items.statement: Term volumes down sharply; third-party regas (tolling) volumes up, now >2/3 of throughput; pattern continuing in Q2 so far
items.quote: the pattern and trend continues as it was in the Q1 of this financial year till so far. However, we expect the issues at the Gulf to resolve soon and the volumes from our long-term contract with Qatar should start immediately

items.statement: Deepak Fertilizers contract started May 2026, 2 cargoes delivered in Q1; ExxonMobil volumes at Kochi also commenced
items.quote: Both contracts have actually started taking place and we have brought in volumes. Volumes have been brought in by both the parties under both these contracts.

items.statement: Dahej regas tariff ~INR 69/MMBtu; Kochi ~INR 98/MMBtu for current quarter; no tariff revision discussions ongoing
items.quote: Dahej is around INR69 and Kochi is around INR98.

items.statement: Offtaker contract renewals in daily discussions; closure expected in next 2-3 quarters ahead of new Qatar contract starting 2028
items.quote: We can expect it to happen in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Time charter vessels suspended under contract clauses (not force majeure); no charter hire payable during suspension
items.quote: all the time charter vessels, we have suspended the operation as per not under any force majeure clause, but there are other clauses in the contract, other in the time charter agreements through which we have enabled the suspension.

items.statement: Petrochemical plant useful life assumed at 25 years; equity IRR not recalculated pending remaining commercial contracts
items.quote: These kinds of projects generally take we generally people take a 25 years' life.

items.statement: INR 70-75 crore capex in FY27 for new Jharkhand and Karnataka units (INR 100 crore total); adds INR 350 crore revenue potential by FY29
items.quote: About INR70 crores to INR75 crores is estimated to be spent in this current financial year. In a steady state, these 2 facilities will add revenue to the extent of almost INR350 crores.

items.statement: Plans to add 2,000-3,000 machines by end of FY27 (operational FY28); each 1,000 machines yields ~INR 200 crore revenue
items.quote: I would like to add at least 2,000, 3,000 machines extra by the end of this year, additional -- those will probably come into operations by later half of next financial year.

items.statement: ETR expected to decline to 20-22% by end of FY27 from current ~25% due to international operations contribution
items.quote: We estimate ETR between 20% and 22% for this year.

items.statement: Broad-based customer interest across categories (shirts, bottoms, denims); India gaining traction in Bangladesh-type products via low-cost regions
items.quote: Today, I'm seeing even people are looking at India for shirts and bottoms where there are typical Bangladesh category products, and they are looking at low-cost regions within India.

items.statement: Wage costs rose INR 20 crore in Q1 (Haryana 35%, Karnataka 5%); absorbed via automation, productivity, rupee depreciation (hedged at INR 89), and pricing
items.quote: In Q1 of this year, our India business saw a salary wage cost increase of INR20 crores and that has been absorbed in the system.

items.statement: Drum Closure segment achieved highest ever 43% EBIT margin in Q1 FY27 driven by higher volumes and rupee depreciation; management guides sustainable margin upwards of 30%
items.quote: So, volumes is the main thing. This has been our highest revenue as well as EBIT margin and absolute EBIT ever for the segment and the sales, the quantity that has been sold as , has been higher. The rupee depreciation has also contributed because, Drum Closures majority, almost 100% of our revenue is export.

items.statement: No significant new capex planned for FY27; only maintenance capex. Phase 2 of CSN plant capacity expansion targeted for FY28
items.quote: This year, there is no significant new CAPEX, only maintenance CAPEX across all the divisions. Next year is when we would be looking to commission our Phase 2 in our CSN plant, where we would probably be looking to add some more capacity to the Extrusion plant and forward integration.

items.statement: Scaffolding demand strong in US driven by AI chip, semicon and energy plant construction; visibility for at least next 2 quarters
items.quote: We are quite comfortable that at least the foreseeable next 2 quarters, we should be able to maintain or even better the kind of volumes of Scaffolding that we have seen in the first quarter.

items.statement: Mach One (Aluminium Formwork) demand environment very strong across 7 major Indian cities; residential, commercial, GCCs and data centers driving inquiries
items.quote: Right. No, the demand environment is very strong. India, the overall project launches, which is what is we track, which directly correlates to our demand is quite strong across all the 7 major cities across the country.

items.statement: Aluminium Extrusion plant running at 100% capacity since March quarter; helped navigate aluminum price increase and improved segment EBIT

items.statement: Minda VAST margin improved from 6.5% to 8.4% YoY in Q1, target to reach Minda Corp margin levels
items.quote: in quarter one previous year, it delivered a margin of 6.5%, and this quarter it has delivered a margin of 8.4%. Overall, I think we are very happy with the performance of Mindavast, and we are continuously working to see how we can bring it at par with overall Minda Corporation's margin level for Mindavast too.

items.statement: Commodity and labor cost pressures partially offset by operational efficiency and operating leverage; back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers
items.quote: Most of our index commodities have a back-to-back arrangement with our customer. It could have some bit of lag for a quarter or two, but we do have arrangements with the customer.

items.statement: Group capacity utilization at 77-80% depending on plant/product line
items.quote: on an average you can say typically our group capacity is at about 77% to about 80% depending on a particular plant or depending on a particular product line.

items.statement: Sunroof business customer trials approved in first go, SOP on track for Q2 FY27
items.quote: the product customer trials have already been done. They have been approved in the first go itself. So yes, that is completely on track.

items.statement: Targets INR 900-1,000 crore revenue for FY27 and 15-20% growth in FY28; aims for 6% PAT margin in FY27 improving by 75-100 bps in FY28
items.quote: The pace at which we are going as of now, we expect that the revenue or top line we will be closing somewhere in between the INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores mark. This is what is the expectation for FY'26-'27. And we foresee a growth of around 15% to 20% in FY'27-'28 over the current year's figure or current year's re

items.statement: Reaffirms medium-term aspiration of INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY28 with 32-35% CAGR from FY25-29
items.quote: As shared earlier, our medium-term aspiration remains to achieve approximately INR1,000 crores in revenue by financial year 2028, with a target revenue CAGR of 32% to 35% between financial year 2025 and financial year 2029.

items.statement: Commissioned new soap line at Roorkee adding 1,700 MT/month; aggregate FMCG capacity now 20,840 MT/month; minimal capex expected for next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: we commissioned a new soap production line at our existing Roorkee facility, adding approximately 1,700 metric ton of monthly capacity, taking our aggregate FMCG and FMCG intermediary capacity to 20,840 tons per month from 19,640 tons per month.

items.statement: Targets consolidated EBITDA margin improvement of 2-2.5% from current levels by FY28; aims for 7% PAT margin by FY28
items.quote: So with regard to EBITDA margin, the current quarter number will go up definitely in the future, right? And with regard to profitability also, we can say that because we are aiming a target of 7% by FY'28, so definitely the EBITDA margin will also go up by another 2% to 2.5% from here.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions kept crude and derivatives volatile, impacting dyes, chemicals, fuel, LABSA, and PP packaging costs; textile business most affected; expects normalization by Q3/Q4 FY27
items.quote: We believe that by Q3 or Q4 things will get normalized because Q2 we are seeing the impact of this situation again.

items.statement: Strong broad-based demand across FMCG, FMCG intermediate, and edible businesses; FMCG now ~90.6% of revenue vs 83% in FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we continued to witness strong broad-based demand across our FMCG, FMCG intermediate, and edible businesses, which together now contribute approximately 90.60% of our consolidated revenue, up from around 83% for the full year Financial Year 2026.

items.statement: Long-term revenue mix target: 90-92% FMCG, 8-10% textile; food and soap segments expected to drive incremental revenue over next 2 years
items.quote: So, in the longer run, we expect that the textile business will contribute somewhere in between 8% to 10% of the total revenue. Remaining 90% to 92% revenue will come from the FMCG segment.

items.statement: Food (spices, savories) and soap segments expected to contribute most incremental revenue over next two years
items.quote: So, in the coming two years, the revenue from food business as well as from the soap segment is going to be a bit on higher side for next two years.

items.statement: Q1 profitability impacted by higher raw material costs from geopolitical headwinds; priority for next 2-3 quarters is to nullify cost increase impact
items.quote: So, the first and foremost thing is that, with regard to whatever impact which we had in Q1 with regard to profitability, so that is our first and foremost target for coming two to three quarters that we will be just nullifying the impact of cost increase.

items.statement: No plans for additional fundraising; INR 98.65 crore preferential issue funds deployed for Bhilwara food facility and Guwahati soap noodle/cosmetic facility; Roorkee expansion funded from subsidiary retained earnings
items.quote: As of now, we don't have any plan for additional fundraising.

items.statement: Bhilwara food facility (spices, savories) running single shift; second shift available for capacity expansion; B2B model with quarterly planning and monthly firm orders from customers
items.quote: So currently, we are using our plant only for one shift. So almost we can say if required that we have to increase our production, we have second shift completely free for the same.

items.statement: Textile business expected to improve by Q3 FY27; no demerger plans; all revenue currently B2B manufacturing, no B2C brands
items.quote: So by quarter three this year, we are expecting to get good in in textile business also. As of now, we don't have any plan for demerger or that kind of thing.

items.statement: Long-term target of sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margins of 20% or higher (Rule of 50)
items.quote: Our long -term philosophy remains the same, the Rule of 50, the sustained annual revenue growth above 30%, together with EBITDA margins of 20% or higher.

items.statement: Growth driven by direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech, Retail and premium omnichannel formats like CTV and video streaming
items.quote: Growth was led by direct advertiser demand in structurally expanding sectors like Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech, and Retail and by premium omnichannel formats such as connected TV and video streaming.

items.statement: Capital prioritized towards AI stack, international expansion, platform capabilities and selective inorganic opportunities
items.quote: Capital is being prioritized towards AI stack, international expansion and platform capabilities alongside selective inorganic opportunities that add clear capability of market access.

items.statement: Platforms delivered 14.16 million verified outcomes at Rs. 49.94 per outcome in Q1 FY27
items.value: 14.16 million outcomes at Rs. 49.94 per outcome
items.quote: Q1 FY27, our platforms delivered 14.16 million verified outcomes at Rs. 49.94 per outcome.

items.statement: Revenue per outcome improving due to AI technology, shift to higher-value global markets, and premium inventory (CTV, Apple ecosystem)
items.quote: The second important parameter is because we are going in the global markets. Now, the global markets are like they are not a volume driven market, they are a value driven market.

items.statement: Preferential raise of ~Rs. 50 crore in FY26 for strategic acquisitions, technology advancement, and general purposes; disciplined evaluation of inorganic opportunities ongoing
items.quote: We raised capital specifically to pursue some of the strategic acquisitions and we continue to evaluate those opportunities actively.

items.statement: International revenue share at 20.7% in Q1 FY27; US, UK, ASEAN operations scaling; GTM via agency/reseller model first, then direct
items.quote: International markets contributed 20.7% with India being the anchor. As our US, UK and ASEAN operations scale, we expect the international share to build gradually over the coming years.

items.statement: Neural Engine launched: unified AI layer (P3 - Process Signals, Predict Intent, Produce Outcomes) enabling campaign launch in under 59 seconds, decisioning in under 15ms
items.quote: The Neural Engine collapses the advertising lifecycle into a single system, so a markete er can move from planning to a live campaign in under 59 seconds.

items.statement: Direct client revenue share declined to 65.2% from 73.9% due to international agency/reseller expansion; long-term strategy remains direct advertiser approach
items.quote: This is because of the reason that we have entered international global footprint with our initial strategy of going to the clients through agency or a reseller model.

items.statement: Top 5 sectors (FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Travel) contribute 70-80% of revenue; diversification expected from online services, consumer goods, gaming
items.quote: To be very frank, about 75 to 80% of the contribution by the Top 5 sectors, which is which is in FinTech, Quick Commerce, BFSI, Commerce, Retail, Traveling.

items.statement: International growth drivers expected to kick in over next 12-18 months; emerging markets (Asia, LatAm) and developed markets (US, UK) targeted
items.quote: We have a roadmap of next 12 to 18 months in terms of increasing our penetration both in evolved and the emerging markets.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 revised to 30-40% from earlier 40-50%
items.quote: So, while we already have substantial order in hand, we would like to stay at about 30% to 40% as a guiding number, so as to give you an insight about at the level at which we would grow.

items.statement: Order book stands at 2.16 GW valued at Rs 2,250 crore as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our current order book of 2.16 Gigawatt, valued at over Rs. 2,250 crores, provides us with strong revenue visibility.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted to ~20% in Q1 FY27 from 28% in Q4 FY26 due to geopolitical, fuel/logistics, and ROW cost pressures
items.quote: A gross margin in Q1 FY27 was approximately 20% compared with that at 28% in Q4 FY26. This is a sequential contraction of approximately 8 percentage points.

items.statement: India added record 6.05 GW wind capacity in FY26; long-term decarbonization targets support strong demand outlook
items.quote: India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in FY26, taking cumulative installed wind capacity beyond 56 GW.

items.statement: Internal target to complete substantial portion of order book in FY27; cautious 30-40% guidance reflects on-ground uncertainties
items.quote: While our internal targets are definitely to have completed the substantial portion of the order book that we have on hand, but the scenario that we are giving right now is a bit cautious scenario considering the on ground situation.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin to reach upward of 20% for full year FY27
items.quote: We are strongly confident as per our estimate to see EBITDA margin of upward to 20% on to the whole year basis.

items.statement: Shalby International Gurgaon unit occupancy expected to reach 30%+ by Q3/Q4 FY27 with PBT breakeven near Q3 end/Q4
items.quote: we do expect our occupancy level to touch 30% or up from Quarter 3 or Quarter 4 onwards and we are also likely very confident that on to the Quarter 4 or near Quarter 3 end, we would be able to see a PBT positive number also

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE expected to improve to industry standard 11-13% within 1-2 years from current ~7%
items.quote: we would expect that to fall in the within industry standard from 1 to 2 years from here which is between 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Gross margins in MedTech expected to increase 100-200 basis points each quarter going forward
items.quote: we are confident to see a better bottom line in the subsequent quarter also importantly by the reason of the upside on to our gross margins which is expected to increase about 100 basis to 200 basis points each quarter from here on

items.statement: Hospital EBITDA margin pressure is temporary; new doctor deployments and TPA renewals to drive improvement in subsequent quarters
items.quote: The pressure on the EBITDA margin is temporary because we have deployed new doctors and new specialties which had come in so it takes some time about a quarter or so that the doctor reflects of its complete profitability into the subsequent quarter we see the EBITDA margin to improve

items.statement: New TPA renewals underway with potential 5-7% revenue upside from renewals and tie-ups in active discussion
items.quote: new TPA renewals are also actively underway which would give a significant upside on to the renewal which holds a potential of 5% to 7% jump on to our revenue with the TPAs and other tie-ups which are in active discussion

items.statement: Minimal capex planned for FY27 as major investments (bunker facility, robotics, MedTech) already deployed in recent years
items.quote: we would be able to manage with a minimal CAPEX since we have already invested that and EBITDA positive into our Gurgaon unit

items.statement: MedTech India revenue grew 98% YoY and 29% QoQ to ~₹36 crores in Q1 FY27 reflecting strong product traction
items.quote: Shalby MedTech limited at India level which delivered a revenue of approximately ₹36 crores registering a growth of 29% sequentially and a 98% on year-on-year basis

items.statement: MedTech consolidated EBITDA positive for 4th consecutive quarter at ~₹1.7 million; India entity EBITDA grew 191% QoQ to ~₹22.9 crores
items.quote: Our India level entity reported approximately ₹22.9 Cr compared ₹2.9 Cr revenue as compared to ₹10 million in Quarter 4 of the FY 26 with ₹12.8 million in Q1 '26. This represents an approximately growth of 191% sequentially

items.statement: Mobile phone manufacturing trial production by Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28; first year 8M units, doubling to 15-16M in year 2
items.quote: On timeline, we are on course to commence the trial production by quarter 4 of FY '27 and commercial production to begin quarter 1 of FY '28. On the scale front, we expect to begin with around 8 million units in the first year, followed by a calibrated phase-wise ramp-up and expect to double to almost about 15 million,

items.statement: Railway Sub-system & Defense division expected to deliver 30-35% revenue growth in FY27 with margins of 15-16%
items.quote: On the revenue front, 30% to 35% looks doable. And the margins in this financial year, we look at around in the range of 15% to 16% for this division.

items.statement: Consumer Durable division expected to grow in line with RAC industry at 13-15% in FY27
items.quote: It can vary from like between -- it should range between 13% to 15%. So we are in line to that.

items.statement: Electronics division maintains 40%+ revenue growth guidance for FY27
items.quote: As guided earlier, we hope that we will be able to deliver that number.

items.statement: HDI PCB facility at Jewar (INR3,200 cr) and multilayer PCB at Hosur (INR1,000 cr) under construction; AC mega plant construction to start FY28, trial production by FY29
items.quote: We have already announced a capex of close to about INR3,200 crores in Jewar and about INR1,000 crores in Hosur. The plant will be up and running this financial year of Hosur. And for Jewar, it will take about 18 months from now for the trial production to start.

items.statement: IL JIN fire disruption: permission to reconstruct received, adequately insured, business shifted to other locations, minimal impact expected
items.quote: We have received permission to reconstruct the facility just yesterday from the departments. So the assessment is undergoing, and we will intimate the exchanges. items.statement: IL JIN Board approved fundraising up to INR5,000 cr; quantum and structure to be finalized
items.quote: We have given the clarification that we'll be raising up to INR5,000 crores. So we'll tell you that by -- whenever we finalize that how much fundraise is happening, we'll update everyone that how much is the fund raise.

items.statement: Festive season demand muted due to regulatory changes (tonnage labeling); strong summer expected from November post inventory liquidation by Diwali
items.quote: We are expecting this inventory to be liquidated. Post that, we see that the market to be at equalized level. And we expect a strong summer starting from November month. So we are not expecting very, very high demand on this coming festive season.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consumer durable margin benefited from premium product mix (5-star, 2-ton) and pre-stocking of compressors/copper; not sustainable for full year
items.quote: So whatever products we have made are majorly on the 5-star category and the 2-tonne category. So because of that, the realization of the margins are better. But every quarter, this mix keeps on changing. I think the better is to see on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt increased to INR1,225 cr (June '26) from INR510 cr (March '26)
items.quote: The net debt level as on 30th June is around INR1,225 crores. And last year, March '26, it was around INR510 crores.

items.statement: Overall margins normalized at current levels if no further currency/commodity disruption; earlier guidance of 50-100 bps decline revised
items.quote: We were earlier expecting 50 to 100 bps. But now we think that these margins are normalized at where we are in case there is no further disruption in the currency and commodity.

items.statement: Fluoropolymers expected to grow 17-20% annually going forward, driven by volume and high-value products
items.quote: Fluoropolymers has done well and expected to grow, as we had said earlier, 17% to 20% annually going forward as well, again, primarily on volume as well as the high- value products.

items.statement: Battery materials revenue to reach 3-digit crores by Q4 FY27 with significant ramp-up in FY28
items.quote: We are on track and meeting our targets, what you said, 3 digit in quarter 4 and significant ramp-up in the following financial year.

items.statement: Gross block expected to reach INR 1,200 crores by end of FY27 from current INR 836 crores
items.quote: But we expect, by the end of this year, these numbers to be around INR 1,200 crores.

items.statement: Chemical segment EBITDA margin improved from 26% in Q4 FY26 to 29% in Q1 FY27 due to higher volumes, improved mix and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 26% in Q4 FY26 to 29% in Q1 FY27, reflecting the benefits of higher volumes , improved product mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: Marginal price increases taken to pass through input cost inflation; formula-based pricing protects margins
items.quote: There has been a marginal price increase to come back with whatever input prices have taken place. But however, whatever price increases, small, we have taken, it's going to reflect and the value-added products, which we have taken where we are going for newer applications, that will start reflecting in subsequent quar

items.statement: Strong demand across fluoropolymers driven by semiconductors, data centers, electronics, automotive, green hydrogen and advanced industrial applications
items.quote: The expansion of new-age applications is creating attractive growth opportunities, particularly in areas such as semiconductors, data centers, electronics, automotive, green hydrogen and advanced industrial applications.

items.statement: Oman battery materials project put on hold due to geopolitical delays; capacities being relocated to India with separate funding
items.quote: The Oman project right now, we have put on hold, okay? And we are -- in fact, what we are doing is that those capex is now -- we are bringing it to India and planning to add those capacities in India. And there are multiple reasons for it. There have been certain, of course, geopolitical reasons, which was causing cert

items.statement: Fundraise process ongoing for India battery materials expansion after Oman sovereign funding becomes unavailable
items.quote: We are already -- our fundraise process is on, and we are raising as we are going along in terms of our fund requirement. Clearly, the fund in Oman was raised with a -- very specific to Oman project, okay? Now coming back to India, we will, I think, continue to raise funding for these projects.

items.statement: AHF capacity expansion in phases: first phase by end of FY27/Q3, subsequent phases matched to refrigerant capacity additions
items.quote: It will be in different phases. The first set of capacities will be there probably by the end of this year or the third quarter. And then subsequently, every quarter, some capacity will be added because it will be matched with our refrigerant capacity being added.

items.statement: R32 expansion expected to reach full utilization of 20,000 tons during calendar year 2027
items.quote: Yes, we expect full utilization. Based on our understanding of the market, as and when we have the capacities, we are looking at able to market it, full utilization of R32.

name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd

items.statement: Catering margins traditionally between 10% to 12%; proof-of-concept impact of INR4 crore to die down by Q3; one-time HR cost of INR20 crore booked in Q1 will not repeat
items.quote: So this is one, and proof of concept will slowly die down. There are two trains I think they will finish by September and the remaining two trains will finish by November. So that way it will help and the catering margin traditionally have been between 10 % to 12%. So we will try to maintain that.

items.statement: 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected in FY27 or next year; license fee calibrated at INR6 crore per train totalling ~INR120 crore
items.quote: But whenever there is a passenger growth, the trains, normally there may be around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains introduced in this financial year or the period of next one year. So, the license fee of this can be calibrated to around INR6 crores per train to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Internet ticketing EBITDA margin 80.33% in Q1 FY27 vs 84.12% YoY; decline due to NGET infra refresh (~INR150 crore), INR10 crore maintenance, upcoming active-active disaster recovery at Secunderabad
items.quote: Normally, it remains between 80% to 85%, so it is, like you have seen, it is around 80% this time. These are some of the reasons which I would like to share with you.

items.statement: Rail Neer margin fell from 14% to 10% YoY due to ~30% resin cost increase (petroleum/West Asia crisis); material cost rose INR55 cr to INR61 cr
items.quote: Due to the increase of petroleum product due to West Asia crisis, the material cost increased from INR55 crores to INR61 crores. There was a dip of INR6 crores. You have seen that the margin has gone from 15 to 11.

items.statement: E-catering meals grew from 1.05 lakh/day to 1.69 lakh/day; e-catering revenue rose from INR16 cr to INR22 cr; election specials revenue jumped from INR5 cr to INR41 cr
items.quote: E-catering is another growing segment which has grown to around INR1.05 lakh meals from '25 to '26 to INR1.69 lakh meals in financial '26-'27. And e-catering revenue has grown by INR6 crores from INR16 crores to INR22 crores.

items.statement: Vande Bharat catering via empanelled service providers (limited tender); 81 Vande Bharats currently served by IRCTC; shift to sleeper Vande Bharat will increase catering lead and capacity
items.quote: In Vande Bharat also we have got empanelled service providers, for which we float a limited tender and then we give it out as far as the catering is concerned.

items.statement: AGEasy expected to reach contribution breakeven by Q4 FY27 (January 2027) and EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27
items.quote: As we look ahead, we remain committed to profitability. As I said, AGEasy perhaps by January or last quarter of this year will be in that zone.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue trajectory to continue growing substantially in FY27 while EBITDA losses get contained as no new beds are being added
items.quote: This trajectory will continue for FY27 in terms of revenue going up substantially and EBITDA losses getting contained because now we are not adding any new beds at this point of time.

items.statement: Antara Noida Phase I: 340 units offered possession in June 2026, INR169 crores demand raised, ~75% collected as of August 2026
items.quote: We raised a demand of about INR169 crores with the offers of possession. INR30-odd crores were collected within June, but the rest has now come, most of it in July and August. As on date, approximately 75% of total dues have been collected.

items.statement: Antara Noida Phase II approval next focus; current prices INR16,000-18,000+ vs Phase I average INR7,000-10,000
items.quote: the rates have moved significantly up, and they are in the range of INR16,000, INR18,000 plus. So hopefully, when we launch Phase II, we should be able to realize the profits as well.

items.statement: Dehradun expansion: <150 units on new land parcel, potential sales value INR850-900 crores
items.quote: We have found a small piece of land. It might be just less than 150 units. But given the sales price we are commanding, the sales value will be again INR850 crores to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity recovered: 27 units in Q1 FY27, 34 units in July 2026, similar trend in August
items.quote: while we sold only 27 units in Q1 FY27, in the month of July alone, we sold about 34 units and a similar trend continues in August. So we have caught up.

items.statement: Care Homes: 4 of 8 homes achieved highest ever ARPOB of INR7,000+ in June 2026; 3 of 4 show significant contribution margin improvement
items.quote: Happy to also report that 4 of our Care Homes achieved an ever highest ARPOB, which is average revenue per occupied bed day of INR7,000 plus in June '26.

items.statement: Blended ARPOB expected near INR7,500 as occupancy rises across Care Homes
items.quote: It should be near INR7,500.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 2,355M; like-to-like projects grew 12% YoY
items.quote: Our revenue grew approximately 22% year-on-year in Q1. More importantly, our like-to-like projects grew approximately 12%.

items.statement: Retail business (RPL) expected to turn EBITDA positive by Q2 FY27
items.quote: by Q2, we expect RPL to also be EBITDA positive. And from there on, it will continue it's upward journey.

items.statement: Retail revenue contribution target 10-15% of total revenue by end of FY27
items.quote: Our contribution what we are looking to target this financial year is to be in the range of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Awarded Himachal Pradesh CT project for 34 CT scans across state, predominantly cash-paying, 10-year visibility
items.quote: Krsnaa has recently been awarded the Himachal Pradesh CT project for 34 CT scans across the entire state. items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR588 million with an EBITDA margin of 25% against 27% in Q1 FY26. items.statement: Retail revenue grew 64% YoY to INR 193M (9% of group revenue); network expanded to 4,000+ touchpoints across 7 states
items.quote: Our retail revenue for the Q1 FY27 stood at INR193 million against revenue of INR118 million in quarter 1 FY'26, growing at impressive year-on-year growth rate of 64% and contributed approximately 9% of overall group revenue.

items.statement: Promoter warrant infusion for capex on projects and potential acquisitions
items.quote: Two reasons. One is, of course, the funds will be utilized for certain capital expenditure for projects and certain acquisitions that we have in mind, and that was the reason why the funds have been raised.

items.statement: Fees to hospitals expense rose to INR 41 crore in Q1 due to Rajasthan project partner revenue-sharing arrangements
items.quote: the actual increase is on account of Rajasthan project. So for a project like Rajasthan or even other PPP projects, we have certain partners that we work in these remote locations. And there's a certain revenue share amount that goes to these partners.

items.statement: FY27 guidance unchanged; confident of achieving full-year targets backed by strong launch lineup and project completion visibility
items.quote: Our guidance remains unchanged. We remain confident of achieving our full year guidance. The confidence is primarily underpinned by the strong launch lineup and the project completion visibility.

items.statement: FY27 sales value guidance INR 3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth); collections guidance INR 2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth)
items.quote: In our FY27 outlook, we have given a sales value growth of almost 40% to 50%, up to INR3,300 crores to INR 3,500 crores, whereas the corresponding collection figure is much muted at a 26% to 30% growth of INR2,100 crores to INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: FY27 PBT margin expected 8-9%; FY28 PBT margin target ~10%
items.quote: So, this year, we might be in the 8% to 9%. And as I said earlier in the past, we would have at least a 20% growth in our revenue recognition and therefore, from last year.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA margin target 22-24%
items.quote: What I would like to say is, our EBITDA margin should be in the range of about 22% to 24% by FY28.

items.statement: FY28 mission: sales value ~INR 5,000 crores, revenue ~INR 2,500 crores, PBT ~INR 250 crores
items.quote: We are on track towards achieving our FY28 mission. The current pipeline provides substantial visibility for this objective.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity may rise temporarily in FY27 but long-term comfort zone 0.5x; gross debt INR 651 crores, net debt INR 432 crores as of June
items.quote: So, if I look at our overall gearing, it will go up. It would most likely go up during FY 27. The gearing can rise temporarily, because as you know, as we are pursuing aggressive growth and trying to lock more project pipeline, understandably, either equity or debt has to come in, not only the cash from operation.

items.statement: Q1 margins muted due to ~40% revenue from low-margin legacy Kolkata projects; margins expected to improve in H2 as higher-margin products complete
items.quote: The muted margins are largely product mix driven rather than structure, with around 40% from relatively lower margin legacy projects from Kolkata. Margins are expected to improve in H2 and higher-margin product reaches completion.

items.statement: Sustenance sales prices rising 4-5% annually; launch prices set per micro-market competition; no large post-COVID style 10-15% jumps expected
items.quote: On the pricing side, I don't see a big jump in price. I just want to clarify. So like the post-COVID, we saw like 10%, 15% annual increase. That may not happen. On an average, we are seeing roughly about 4%, 5% increase in selling price.

items.statement: Underlying demand strong across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata; mid-market end-use demand resilient; conversion rates stable; no material slowdown in housing loan applications
items.quote: We are not seeing on ground where customers are backtracking. We haven't seen the conversion rate going down in a material way. Therefore, we are of the belief and even my industry checks with housing loan companies, they are not seeing any slowdown in application momentum.

items.statement: Strategy: premiumization (Chennai premium launch Shriram Stellar 20% sold in launch weekend) and product diversification (Kolkata plotted development 55% sold in 30 days); mid-market ASP up from ~INR 5,000 to ~INR 7,600-7,700/sqft
items.quote: With Shriram Stellar, we have entered Chennai's premium residential segment with our premium offering. Around 20% of the project was sold during the first weekend of the launch, validating the product positioning with our brand distinct.

items.statement: Launch calendar back-ended (Q3/Q4) creating collection timing gap; Kolkata 2.3 msf apartment approvals to be phased; Pune Manjari launch dependent on local approvals; gearing may rise temporarily
items.quote: Since they are all Q3, Q4 launches, they will not translate exactly into the same amount of collections. And so this year, based on the progress of current ongoing projects and the timing of launches of our five or six launches that we are targeting in Q3 and Q4, we expect the collection to be in the range of about INR

items.statement: H2 handover pipeline: >2,900 units with INR 1,560 crores revenue potential; 410 units (INR 400 cr) ready now, 400+ units (INR 160 cr) targeting OC in Q2, 2,100+ units (INR 1,000 cr) targeting OC in H2
items.quote: Overall, more than 2,900 units representing over INR1,560 crores of revenue potential are scheduled for handover and revenue recognition during the balance of the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27: highest ever Q1 sales INR 484 crores (0.85 msf, +10% YoY); collections INR 365 crores (+8% YoY); 690 units handed over; free cash flow before new investment INR 135 crores; net free cash flow INR 47 crores; cash balance INR 219 cro
items.quote: We achieved our highest ever Q1 sales of INR 484 crores with sales volume of 0.85 million square feet. Collections were INR 365 crores, supported by execution and handovers.

items.statement: Expect full year FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: As shared earlier, we expect full year EBITDA margins to be broadly in line with last year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering clear step-up in FY27 full year growth given strong Q1 start
items.quote: Looking ahead, given the strong start in Q1, we are confident of delivering a clear step-up in our FY27 full year growth.

items.statement: FY30 ambition remains 2x revenue from FY25 and 3x EBITDA in same period
items.quote: Our ambition of 2x revenue from FY25 to FY30 and 3x EBITDA in the same period remains the North Star for us, and we remain confident of delivering that.

items.statement: ESOP expense expected in range of INR25-26 crores for FY27
items.quote: We expect ESOP to be in the range of INR25 crores to INR26 crores. We should be in that range.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.5%, down 46 bps YoY due to gross margin moderation and higher growth investments
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 10.5%, a decline of 46 basis points year-on-year, primarily due to a moderation in gross margins and our planned and deliberately higher growth investments.

items.statement: Gross margin at 58.4% in Q1 FY27, down 131 bps YoY due to higher commodity costs and adverse currency
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 58.4%, lower by 131 basis points year-on-year, reflecting the impact of higher commodity costs and adverse currency movements.

items.statement: AMC price increases of 3-12% implemented, led to some deferral in renewals but expect normalization over time
items.quote: The price increase, the band was roughly between 3% to 12%.

items.statement: Product price hikes taken at start of Q1, peers followed with lag; now at price equilibrium with competitors
items.quote: The price increase that we took, our peers followed albeit with a lag with almost similar price increases. Though like I said, there was a lag and of roughly a 30-day period when we had pricing ahead of the others. But now as things stand today, there is again price equilibrium versus competitors.

items.statement: No further consumer price hikes planned currently; bias towards not disturbing growth momentum, will drive efficiencies instead
items.quote: At this point in time, we are going to be more measured as far as consumer price increase is concerned because we see a very, very strong tailwind as far as growth is concerned and our bias will be towards not disturbing that.

items.statement: Service AMC bookings softer due to price hike deferral; expect Q2 service revenue growth similar to Q1, visibility beyond depends on bookings and filter business scale-up
items.quote: Given that there is a relative softness that we've seen and these are initial signs that we've seen as far as AMC bookings are concerned, that impact would play out towards the later part of the year.

items.statement: A&SP spends to increase ahead of revenue growth in FY27, focused on in-store presence and consumer finance adoption
items.quote: At an overall year level, we do expect our A&SP spends to be ahead of revenue growth. So that is something that we are planning for.

items.statement: Launched 4-year filter life products (Glow 4X, Ritz Pro 4X) 45 days ago, first in market, met with very positive response
items.quote: More recently, about 45 days ago, we were the first in the country to launch water purifiers with a four-year life. We launched two products in e-commerce, Glow 4X and Ritz Pro 4X with stainless steel, priced at roughly INR22,000 and INR25,000 respectively. And they've met with a very, very positive response.

items.statement: Management expects to reach EBITDA breakeven by next year (FY28).
items.quote: So I would say that by next year, we will actually come to the breakeven thing, okay?

items.statement: Management reiterates prior commitment to EBITDA breakeven by H2 FY28.
items.quote: Presently, I would say that I would stick to what we have committed last time. If it happens earlier, for sure, we will also announce the same.

items.statement: Railway lounge capex ranges from INR 1.5 crore to INR 5-6 crore per lounge depending on size and location.
items.quote: So it depends from INR1.5 crores going up to maybe INR5 crores to INR6 crores is the capex investment right now.

items.statement: Railway lounge opportunity estimated at INR 500 crores over next 5 years driven by government railway modernization.
items.quote: And this INR500 crores in the next 5 years is very much possible considering that kind of investment.

items.statement: Non-airport lounge services contributed ~33% of revenue in Q1 FY27, a significant diversification milestone.
items.quote: Our non -airport lounge services contributed approximately 33% of the top line during the quarter.

items.statement: Global lounge margins currently similar to legacy domestic lounge margins; expected to improve as volumes scale.
items.quote: Presently, you would not see a better margin compared to what it was earlier. But eventually, I would say that, yes, the margins would get better for Global.

items.statement: Revenue drop in Q1 FY27 driven by sharp decline in Middle East outbound traffic due to war.
items.quote: The drop is drastically because of the war which is happening. So yes, internationally, the traffic is down, and that is one of the biggest reasons that why there is a drop in the revenue.

items.statement: India credit card transaction value expected to grow from ~INR 21 trillion in FY25 to ~INR 54 trillion in FY30 (CAGR ~21%).
items.quote: India's credit card transaction value is expected to grow from approximately 21 trillion in FY 25 to 54 trillion in FY 30, representing a CAGR of around 21%.

items.statement: Signed 3 large APAC banking clients (Singapore, Indonesia) with programs going live in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: We have a very large (card) network in Singapore, where we have already signed up and our program would be going live hopefully by end of this month or early next month. Our second one is in Indonesia, one of the largest bank in Indonesia. Also, we have also gone live there.

items.statement: No current plans for promoter stake increase or strategic investor fundraising; focus remains on business execution.
items.quote: Presently, I think there is no such plans in the promoter group because presently, I think the focus is completely on how to bring the business back into where we were.

items.statement: Cash increased to INR 193.3 crores (from INR 149 crores) due to ~INR 40+ crores collections from receivables.
items.quote: There has been significant efforts in terms of collections. So you are right, there has been like collection of nearly INR40-plus crores, which is there from different customers.

items.statement: No further Minimum Guarantee (MMG) payments expected going forward; gross margins should turn positive.
items.quote: However, going forward, like there will be no such payment. So anyways, you will see positive margins.

items.statement: Employee costs (including ESOPs) expected to remain at current quarter run-rate; full-year ESOP impact only INR 14 lakhs.
items.quote: So if we talk about on a full year basis, the impact of those ESOPs which are issued is only INR14 lakhs. So that is not at all impacting. items.statement: Expect normalized demand trajectory through later part of FY27 after GST-related lumpiness last year
items.quote: While these dynamics are largely behind us, we expect a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of the year.

items.statement: Capex guided at ~INR50 crore for FY27, Q1 spend below proportionate share
items.quote: Our capex, which we had guided in the last year closing at around INR50 crores. We are as of now in line. The first quarter, we have spent less than the proportionate share.

items.statement: Premium and mass segments growing faster than luxury segment in recent months post GST cuts
items.quote: Due to various macro factors and post the GST cuts, we have seen that the premium and mass segments have grown faster than the luxury segment over the last few months.

items.statement: Syros EV receiving healthy order bookings across India, new Sorento launch expected in September
items.quote: The recently launched Syros EV has also received a very healthy order bookings across India. The new Sorento is expected to be launched in September.

items.quote: We have signed an MoU with ChargeZone, one of India's leading EV charging networks. Under this partnership, our EV customers will receive wallet credit redeemable at ChargeZone's charging locations, while we will earn a share of charging revenue from onboarded customers.

items.statement: Mercedes average selling price increased to ~INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27 from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have seen this reflecting in our average selling price, which has increased to approximately INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27, which is up from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA to CFO conversion ~95% (0.95x) maintained, similar to last 2 years
items.quote: Cash flow last year, it was 0.95%. We will be around that only.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 900-950 crore, implying ~50% YoY growth from FY26
items.quote: And the whole year revenue, we are looking at the same at par revenue, which was in FY'2024-2025, that is of the order of Rs. 900 crores to Rs. 950 crores.

items.quote: If in percentage terms we were to explain Q2 would be about 30% to 35% higher than Q1 and thereafter you will see a growth of more than 50% quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target ~25% and PAT margin ~15% for FY27

items.quote: It is Rs. 2329 crores as of now.

items.statement: No capex plans for FY27 as of now
items.quote: As far as any CAPEX plans are concerned there is no such CAPEX plan as of yet.

items.quote: We are bidding in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. And any projects that we see, we are exploring some projects in Maharashtra and Karnataka also.

items.quote: we will see margins come back very quickly to the 20-plus percent mark first. items.quote: MICE will account for anywhere between 20% to maybe -- on an annual basis, 20%, you might have quarters where it tends to be closer to 25%, but that's about it. It's not that more than 50% of the business would come from MICE.

items.statement: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) ongoing across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman, SEC; no fixed timeline given regulatory complexity
items.quote: having seen how regulators in different markets behave, it's very hard to give an exact timeline on that.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps expected vs prior year, above the 100-150 bps annual target
items.quote: this a year where we will clearly do better than that, at least 150 basis points – 200 basis points is what we see us doing you know over last and this year.

items.quote: we've actually taken calibrated price increases towards the end of Q1, we'll be able to offset any such inflationary impact on our procurement perspective.

items.statement: Focus categories contribution rose to ~85% of revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Now the contribution of focus categories has also increased to almost 85%, in Q1FY '27.

items.quote: This year, we were looking at touching approximately INR8,200 crores, INR8,300 crores. So we'll see close to about 20%, 25% growth.

items.quote: We would still be in the region of about 4.3%, 4.4% overall for the -- I mean, when we go to Q3, Q4.

items.quote: As guided during our previous call, we expect the acquired business to achieve sustainable profitability at the PAT level from Q2 onwards.

items.quote: Q2 onwards, we'll see a growth. I wouldn't say 15% growth, which we have guided, but we'll show -- we'll be having a growth of about 6% to 7% in terms of volumes.

items.quote: reported EBITDA increased approximately 87% Y-o-Y to INR71.5 crores, with EBITDA margins improving to 3.8% from 2.9% in Q1 last year.

items.quote: currently, we are at around 4% in terms of PV EBITDA as such. So that should keep inching forward in Q2, Q3 and Q4 with Audi also coming in line.

items.quote: our CV EBITDA percentage because of the CV ticket size, the ticket size of CVs would be about INR16,00,000 on an average. Our EBITDA margins because of that is about 3.6% to 3.7%

items.quote: the tipper segment in commercial vehicles, we are seeing a low to negative growth in terms of Tipper segment. But the small, intermediate, light commercial vehicles, Cargo segment, all are holding good.

items.quote: On the service side, spare parts remains a concern in terms of supply. So there is a short supply on spare parts, and hence, a lot of vehicles getting stuck in the workshops.
