items.quote: NHAI has also outlined a revised FY27 plan to award 54 highways and expressway project covering through 2,444 kilometers worth of combined INR1 .8lakh crores across 13 states so that the near -term awarding environment remains measured.

items.statement: Asset monetization: Sold 2 HAM SPVs to Indus Infra Trust; Ramagiri invested INR83 cr, got INR227 cr; Palani invested INR64 cr, got INR295 cr (incl INR90 cr EPC claim)
items.quote: In KNR Ramagiri, the company has invested INR83 crores in SPV through equity and subordinate debt and received a total consideration of INR227 crores from the purchaser. And for KNR Palani, the company has invested INR64 crores in SPV through equity and subordinate debt and received a consideration of INR295 crores, in

items.statement: Battery storage: Early stage, bids went badly, cautious approach due to dollar/price risk; No revenue guidance
items.quote: Sir, battery storage, initially, we tried some bids. They went ver y bad actually. So, right now, I think we are just preparing some bids, but I'm not very sure of winning a contract because the way things are moving here in India, they are very wrong actually.

items.statement: Domino's household penetration low: 6-7M Indians eat pizza monthly, only 3 occasions per 1,000 meals; massive category growth headroom; focus on growing frequency beyond 3 occasions
items.quote: what are we saying that there are 6 million -7 million Indians who are eating pizza every month, right? So that's a very low number. And even in those 6 million - 7 million out of 1,000 meals they will eat in a year, they will eat it 3 in those 1,000 occasions

items.statement: Targets same growth pace as last two years with healthy margins; may invest margin for growth if ROI favorable
items.quote: Our overall financial year basis target remains the same to continue the same pace of growth that we have demonstrated over the last two years.

items.statement: Positive consumer sentiment seen in August; expects festive demand in Q3/Q4 to improve price elasticity ROI
items.quote: If I am looking at Q2 generally, we are seeing positive consumer sentiment in August, and we hope that this will continue for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Women's wear emerging as growth pillar; targets 2-3x revenue in a year; Dockers license to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters
items.quote: We believe that in the future, women's wear could easily be at least 2x, if not 3x of our revenue in about a year's time, 3x of the current revenue in a year's time, considering the current pace.

items.statement: Wholesale/B2B2C channel now ~40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue (~INR 10 cr in Q1); margin neutral at EBITDA level
items.quote: Wholesale basis revenue now accounts for approximately 40% of the total revenue of Thomas Scott brands, highlighting the growing penetration of our best-selling styles across the aggregator-led route within the marketplaces.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacities fully occupied; adding capacity incrementally; CapEx not high, focused on operational needs like worker training and line efficiency
items.quote: Our manufacturing capacities are fully occupied. So, we largely have to produce in capital capacities, rent out or pay job work and kind of utilize other capacities of other factories.

items.statement: Fire incident last year led to elevated working capital debt; insurance claim of ~INR 21 cr under process; expects debt normalization and interest cost reduction upon settlement
items.quote: We had a fire incident last year where we had about Rs. 21 crore worth of stock covered by insurance fully. Against that, we had to take an elevated level of working capital loans to finance the inventory.

items.statement: Own website contribution increasing due to AI-oriented tech upgrades; sees potential as major future channel
items.quote: Our own website contribution has increased over the last few months, largely driven by certain technology-related uplifts that we have done on our own website and making it an AI oriented website.

items.statement: Offline stores EBITDA positive but ROCE lower than online; capital deployment focused online; selective store expansion may accelerate next financial year
items.quote: Stores have been growing consistently and they are EBITDA positive. But generally, when we look at our return on capital employed, we find better opportunities in what we are doing within the scope of online at the moment.

items.statement: Manufacturing mix steady at ~50% in-house, 35-40% job work, 5% trading; core fast fashion speed (15-45 days) requires in-house control
items.quote: We are looking at about 50% in-house, 40%, 35% odd outsource and 5% outright where we just buy out the goods and trade on it. So, that would largely be consistent.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost typically 4-6% of GMV; higher in Q1 due to marketing spend but offset by higher price points
items.quote: Typically our customer acquisition costs are about 4% to 5%, sometimes 6% of the GMV basis and then the reductions are there. This quarter it would have been a little higher, much higher actually.

items.statement: Trade receivables decreased in Q1 despite higher revenue; insurance receivable claim in final stages, small exception item INR 3-4 lakhs recorded
items.quote: Our trade receivables have decreased this quarter. We have not disclosed it as it is not required as a part of a Q1 disclosure, but it has gone down with higher revenue level over last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order intake of INR 915 crore is the highest ever quarterly order booking; sequential growth in double digits
items.quote: The order is what you see here is the number is INR915 crores. The good part here, the INR 915 crores is the highest ever quarter we booked order in any of the quarter.

items.statement: Order backlog grew ~33% to over INR 2,100 crore entering Q2 FY27
items.quote: Very good news that we still have very strong backlog, which is growth is close to 33% and around INR 2,100 crores plus backlog we are going entering into the Q2.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped due to commodity inflation (copper, transformer wire) impacting legacy orders booked before December with fixed prices
items.quote: When we said legacy orders means the orders which booked before December last year, and these all contracts has a price which we offer to the customer is kind of a firm price because the revision period was somewhere close to 6 months.

items.statement: Negative operating leverage in Q1 due to 5% sales growth vs higher fixed cost inflation (salary increments, 8-10% cost inflation, FX impact)
items.quote: Largely because of operating it started from Q1 and we will hopefully even out throughout the year.

items.statement: Price hike actions initiated timely on standard products; recovery varies by product due to different commodity composition
items.quote: We have initiated the price hike action right at the time when we started witnessing it. And that's the reason why I would not like to comment upon how the competition is doing.

items.statement: Price variation clauses cover only 20-25% of backlog (large projects >6-12 months); mandatory PV clauses now in new contracts but not enforceable in government tenders
items.quote: Historically, I think we -- given this heads up that on price variation clause in the contract, it's in the range of 20%, 25%, not more than that.

items.statement: Capex programs in Baroda (MV factory, transformer factory) and new Kolkata plant on track; staggered completions through CY27 and CY28 with ramp-up thereafter
items.quote: There are many things which are going to happen in calendar year '27. There are a few which is going to get over by '28 and thereafter a ramp-up plan.

items.statement: Healthy opportunity pipeline across emerging segments (data centers, semiconductors) and core Power & Grid; >20% of order book from emerging segments
items.quote: More than 1/5 of what is coming is on this new emerging segment is what we hold in our order bank.

items.statement: Emerging segments (data centers, semiconductors) driving higher project scope with installation/commissioning; transactional mix stable
items.quote: Emerging segments is coming with the higher scope, including installation and commissioning. So from supply, we are also getting into the larger the project execution cycle.

items.statement: Rupee depreciated ~8% YTD; commodity prices (copper, aluminum, steel, labor) rising; FX impact on import costs (10-15% of COGS) partially hedged by exports (10-12% of revenue)
items.quote: At the same time, there are certain headwinds, which all of us are facing and so is our company is also facing is the devaluation of rupee, which has gone down. And also it's about 8% is where the rupee has depreciated since the time we started this year.

items.statement: Confident on full-year FY27 delivery; pricing actions and execution plans initiated; balance 3 quarters expected to be good
items.quote: I'm confident that moving forward, the year, which are balance 3 quarters will be good for us.

items.statement: Export revenue 10-12% of total; Kolkata plant capex aimed at export growth but still in ramp-up phase; no medium-term export % target given
items.quote: Today, our export revenue is in the range of 10% to 12% in the revenue. And you know that the capex we invested in Kolkata largely will cater the export market, which is just starting.

items.statement: Strong macro tailwinds: GDP 6.5-7% for 4 years; per capita electricity consumption to reach 1,800-2,000 kWh by 2030; data center capacity 1.6 to 8 GW by 2030; EV penetration 8% to 30%; Vande Bharat trains 160 to 800
items.quote: Data center capacities, as you know, is going to grow up from 1.6 to about 8 gigawatts by 2030, if not more.

items.statement: Legacy fixed-price orders (pre-December) across Power & Grid segments compressing margins; cannot enforce price variation in government/EPC tenders
items.quote: So while we've taken an action, we can't enforce the price variation in all the government tenders backed by EPC and others. So that's -- we have a challenge there.

items.statement: Target overall growth of roughly 10%, with foreign growth expected to be more pronounced than domestic.
items.quote: In terms of growth, we have set a target of roughly about 10%. It varies for domestic and foreign. In foreign, we would expect a more pronounced growth than the domestic market.

items.statement: Domestic combined ratio target set at 103%, foreign combined ratio target at 95% over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: And we would like to have combined ratio target for domestic book at something like 103 and the foreign book at 95 in line with the global markets.

items.statement: Medium-term goal to achieve 60/40 domestic/international premium mix, long-term aspiration remains 50/50.
items.quote: What we are presently targeting with a medium-term in view is 60/40. But again, our goal will be 60/40, but as I said that domestic market outgrows the global market, so it will be a tough job.

items.statement: Life reinsurance portfolio requires evaluation over a full cycle; reserve strengthening previously impacted results, not an experiment but backed by actuarial analysis.
items.quote: I would suggest that life portfolio needs to be watched over a period of couple of years, because ultimately it continues to remain competitive and one has to watch a particular segment over a cycle rather than a couple of years.

items.statement: Investment book at INR 157,800 crores market value (INR 120,000 crores book value); allocation 73.4% fixed income, ~17% equity, ~8.7% money market.
items.quote: Market value as told is INR157,800 crores. That includes only equity, which is around INR58,000 crores, because debt is kept at cost only in ours as it is held to maturity.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32x as of June 30, 2026 from 3.85x a year ago; management expects gradual decline as growth resumes.
items.quote: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32 as on June 30, 2026, as compared to 3.85 as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrade to 'A' from 'A-' expected in 4-5 years, contingent on IFRS/RBC implementation and business performance.
items.quote: If things go all right, probably one can expect in a period of, say, something like 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Foreign premium target of INR 18,000 crores (historical peak) unlikely in 2 years due to softening rates; may take 3-4 years with focus on ROE over volume.
items.quote: Maybe not in a couple of years because of the significant softening trends, the same exposure is coming at a lesser premium. But maybe not in 2 years, maybe 3 or 4 years.

items.statement: Consolidated profit lower due to subsidiary losses: South Africa INR 287 crores loss, Moscow INR 29 crores loss in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: South Africa, we have shown INR287 crores loss during this quarter, and Moscow some INR29 crores loss from the subsidiary. That has resulted into the lower figure compared to last year in consolidated operating profit.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit EBIT margin growth on standalone basis after steel price recovery
items.quote: we have given guidance, we will be able to grow EBIT margin in the double digit. And post the price recovery, we are confident that double digit margin improvement will keep happening in the future also.

items.statement: Rs.250 Crores already infused in Q4 FY26; another Rs.250 Crores planned in Q3 FY27; total guidance Rs.750 Crores over time
items.quote: we have already infused Rs.250 crores in the last quarter, maybe basically Q4 of the last financial year and we anticipate maybe in Q3, we will infuse another Rs.250 Crores. We are given a guidance of total put together about Rs.750 Crores infusion will happen over a period of time.

items.statement: Engineering volume grew 17% in Q1; demand bullish for next 1-2 quarters; exports up double-digit at 14% of revenue
items.quote: So volume grew about 17%.

items.statement: HCV tipper order book 20-25 units; port deployments at Welspun Anjar (22 trucks), Vizag, Chennai, Wonder Cement (Tuna/Dahej ports)
items.quote: As far as the existing tippers are concerned, we have sold about 20-25 numbers of tippers and the initial feedback is positive. Also, keeping in view the order book, which we have for some of the other products, where we have a confirmed order book

items.statement: Cycle business margin expansion in Q1; targeting at least 200 bps improvement for full year FY27
items.quote: we are hopeful, like we shared maybe at least another 2 basis point in the cycle business, we will be able to improve margin for overall year in the current financial year.

items.statement: L3 autos partially seeded in UP/Bihar for testing; full launch decision pending feedback
items.quote: we have introduced L3 products in quarter one, but in the select markets of UP and Bihar, we are testing those particular vehicles in these market and basis on the feedback that we get from these markets, we will take a call forward on L3 as a product.

items.statement: Maintained FY27 volume growth guidance at 6-8% and raised EBITDA per metric ton guidance to INR 24,000-25,000 from INR 19,000-21,000
items.quote: As regards to our guidance for the full year, we maintain our volume guidance at 6% to 8% for the full-year FY26-27, but I, however, increased the range of the EBITDA per metric ton guidance from the current INR 19,000 to INR 21,000 per metric ton to INR 24,000 to INR 25,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR 252.5 crore, up from INR 135.1 crore YoY; EBITDA per MT improved to INR 35,458 from INR 20,009
items.quote: For quarter one, I'm pleased to inform you all that the EBITDA stood at INR 252.5 crores compared to INR 135.1 crores in Q1 FY26, while EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR 35,458 per metric ton from approximately INR 20,009 per metric ton in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Expect healthy demand through coming quarters driven by India festive season and improving international momentum, but monitoring West Asia geopolitical risks
items.quote: As we look ahead, demand indicators remain encouraging across many of our key markets. With the upcoming festive season in India and improving momentum across several international markets, we expect demand to remain healthy through the coming quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in West Asia creating feedstock volatility, longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs requiring close monitoring
items.quote: While supply side pressures have started easing towards the end of June, the situation remains fluid and recent geopolitical developments have once again introduced volatility across commodity and the logistics markets. Longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs continue to be the areas that requi

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 150 crore, similar to last year, with some front-loaded capacity already commissioned
items.quote: We talked about capex guidance. So I think this year, we will be at about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Specialty Care mix improved, contributing positively to EBITDA per MT growth; new products SimpliX, Galaxy Hearth Biosurf, Everbond gaining traction
items.quote: Specialty Care mix has improved, contributing positively to growth in EBITDA per metric ton, moving us steadily towards objective of improving the quality of our earnings through a richer and more differentiated product mix.

items.statement: Fatty alcohol prices expected to move sideways between INR 2,600-2,800 per kg; no significant jumps or corrections anticipated
items.quote: We do see that there should be some steady state in the prices of fatty alcohol, because it's currently at about INR 2,700, INR 2,800 ship India. We do see that it should move sideways between INR 2,600 to INR 2,800.

items.statement: EPC project in Mexico progressing as planned, on track for commercialization within 12 months; EPC service income recognized in Q1
items.quote: I'm also pleased with the progress being made with our EPC project in Mexico. The project continues to progress as planned, contributing EPC service income during the quarter, and we remain on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.

items.statement: India volumes grew 11% YoY led by double-digit performance segment growth; Tier 1 customer demand recovered; non-Tier 1 and D2C grew near double-digit
items.quote: India, our primary engine grew by an impressive 11% led by double-digit growth in performance segment and high single-digit growth in specialty products. More importantly, we witnessed a recovery in Tier 1 customer demand and the return of positive growth momentum in businesses that have been impacted by reformulations

items.statement: Reformulation risk remains if petrochemical prices fall significantly while oleochemical prices stay elevated; currently balance is favorable
items.quote: I would say that, yes, if the petrochemical prices come down significantly and the alcohol prices remain elevated, like as of today, when we see the balance, we do see that the balance is not significantly concerning, for the reformulation to get aggravated.

items.statement: No acquisition planned in AMET region; focus on debottlenecking and diversifying portfolio to other countries
items.quote: AMET market very clearly, we have already done our capex. We obviously will be -- any capexes that we'll be doing there will be more in terms of certain debottlenecking exercises we'll do investments. There is no acquisition we are planning in AMET for sure.

items.statement: New product pipeline targeting >5% of revenue and contribution margins by 2030; some launches expected next quarter
items.quote: And we do look at all new products, -- this thing is by 2030, they should contribute to almost greater than 5% of our total revenue and our contribution margins.

items.statement: Inorganic growth evaluation ongoing with strict criteria; significant work underway but no announcement yet; will not pursue deals for fear of missing out
items.quote: Yes. So this is something that we are progressing well in terms of the way that we are evaluating, mandate with regard to what can be the targets. but we need to get the right fit. we are very clear that we will not do anything that doesn't meet the criteria that we have set, because anything that we do has to be in li

items.statement: Management aims to sustain double-digit revenue growth over the long term, averaging out quarterly volatility.
items.quote: we have been saying for the past few investor calls that what we have been aiming at to sustain a double-digit growth

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 69.05% in Q1 FY27, up ~3% YoY; management expects margins to remain around current levels but acknowledges pressure at higher volumes.
items.quote: EBITDA percentage of total income was 69.05%, also nearly 3% higher than the corresponding period of FY26

items.statement: Scrap sales contribute 50-55% of e-commerce revenue; mineral blocks and coal auctions are the next largest contributors.
items.quote: almost about 50% to 55% of our e-commerce revenue is coming from scrap sale over the past many years

items.statement: Asset-light strategy maintained; no major capex planned. New verticals (TReDS, EPR, Travel, Coal Exchange) leverage existing digital infrastructure.
items.quote: We also took a decision to remain an asset-light company. So, apart from scaling up existing e-commerce business by aggressively expanding our client footprint, we decided to venture into a limited number of new verticals

items.statement: Coal India linkage auctions (NRS) first batch underway; sector-wise auctions to follow. Critical mineral block allocations (7th tranche) completed.
items.quote: we have won the contract with Coal India for coal linkage auctions. So, the first batch of auctions for the same is underway right now and it is expected to be extended to other sectors

items.statement: MMRPL JV turned profitable in Q1 FY27 driven by higher ELV feedstock from EPR norms and OEM/government incentives; positive outlook expected to continue.
items.quote: For the first time in quite a few number of sequential reporting periods, the venture has shown a positive PAT. This has largely been driven by significantly higher feedstock inflows

items.statement: EPR certificate exchange platform ready but awaiting government notification; no minimum volume guarantee; revenue potential speculative until operational.
items.quote: As on date, everything is happening completely in the dark. Nobody knows as to how many certificates are getting transacted, what is the value of the certificates

items.statement: TReDS platform development complete; awaiting RBI approval; targeting operationalization within FY27. Revenue model primarily transaction-fee based.
items.quote: subject to regulatory approvals being obtained, we should be able to operationalize this sometime during this FY27

items.statement: Travel portal (mstcsmarttravel.in) operational for B2B/PSU segment; partnered with EaseMyTrip initially; B2C rollout pending IATA empanelment.
items.quote: We have partnered with EaseMyTrip because they have been in this sector for quite some time because they are a great aggregator and they were ready to partner with us

items.statement: Exploring setting up own coal/mineral exchange following government policy; multiple exchanges expected; leveraging MSTC's auction credibility and sector experience.
items.quote: MSTC is also exploring various possibilities and the ways and methodologies for establishing its own exchanges

items.statement: Revenue models vary: transaction-fee percentage for some products, event-based fees for others, plus software development/AMC charges.
items.quote: For certain products, it is the percentage of the transaction done and for certain things, it is based on the events only

items.statement: Dividend policy guided by DIPAM norms: minimum 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT, whichever is higher. FY26 dividend already declared, pending AGM approval.
items.quote: Minimum that is 4% of the net worth or 30% of the PAT, whichever is higher. It is the minimum dividend that a government company has to declare

items.statement: Reiterated FY25-FY28 consolidated revenue CAGR of 70-75%, EBITDA CAGR 40-45%, PAT CAGR 35-40%
items.quote: We reiterate our earlier guidance of approximately 70% to 75% consolidated revenue CAGR over FY25 to FY28, supported by the phased commissioning and ramp-up of Bokaro, alongside continued strategic organic growth across our existing verticals.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 12-13% and PAT margin 5-6% by FY28 as scale benefits materialize
items.quote: Over the same period, we expect operating EBITDA and PAT to grow at a CAGR of approximately 40% to 45% and 35% to 40%, respectively, with EBITDA and PAT margins gradually stabilizing at approximately 12% to 13% and 5% to 6% by FY28.

items.statement: Bokaro greenfield project: INR341.6 cr deployed (INR139.2 cr internal accruals + INR202.4 cr long-term debt); color-coated line commissioning in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Importantly, healthy and consistent operating cash flows enabled us to deploy INR139.2 crores of internal accruals towards the expansion, taking total capital deployed to INR341.6 crores.

items.statement: Bokaro color-coated line hot trials underway; asset capitalization expected in Q2 FY27; cold rolling and Galvalume lines to follow over next 6 quarters
items.quote: So, it will be capitalized in Q2. It's not yet started. It's going to be started very, very soon. The hot trials are on, and it will be capitalized in Q2.

items.statement: Rolling mill utilization at 83.5% annualized; pipes & tubes at 40.1% annualized with sequential production increase
items.quote: The rolling mill business achieved an annualized capacity utilization of approximately 83.5%, reflecting healthy demand and stronger volume absorption. While the pipes and tubes business operated at approximately 40.1%, with production increasing sequentially.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 536 bps YoY to 67.9%; EBITDA margin contracted to 20.3% from 21.2% due to fuel price spike from Middle East conflict
items.quote: Gross profit was INR112.7 crores with a gross profit margin expanding by 536 basis points year-on-year to 67.9%. Operating EBITDA increased by 7.1% year-on-year to INR33.7 crores, translating into a margin of 20.3% compared with 21.2% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Steel consumption growing 10%+ vs ~7% GDP; strong government infra spend and private investment driving demand; East India has significant catch-up potential
items.quote: So I -- for the first time in a very long time, we are seeing a higher than GDP increase in steel consumption. So if we look at our GDP growth at about 7%, 7.2%, you add about 3% to 4% of inflation, you're looking at about a 10% odd, 11% odd real growth. But out of that, today, we are actually seeing a 10% plus growth

items.statement: Fuel price volatility from Middle East conflict impacted Q1 EBITDA margin; mitigating via gas price pass-through mechanisms with customers
items.quote: While gross profit margins improved meaningfully, the operating EBITDA margin contracted due to a sharp increase in fuel prices arising from the conflict in the Middle East.

items.statement: Pipes & tubes stable-state utilization capped at 65-70% by FY29; color-coated market risk if domestic suppliers compromise on quality
items.quote: My personal under belief is that in pipes and tubes, stable state utilization of 65% to 70% is at best possible. And that's what we hope to achieve in a stable state by, let's say, FY '29 odd.

items.statement: ROCE 9.5% and ROE 9.4% annualized as of June 2026; transitory low returns due to Bokaro capital deployment pre-commissioning
items.quote: ROCE as of 30th June 2026 stood at 9.5% and ROE at 9.4%, both on an annualized basis. These should be read in the context of the greenfield project.

items.statement: Net debt INR468.9 cr (0.57x D/E); INR202.4 cr long-term borrowings for Bokaro; INR139.2 cr internal accruals deployed
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR468.9 crores at a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57x, of which INR202.4 crores represents long-term borrowings drawn for the Bokaro project.

items.statement: No export focus currently; domestic priority; UK FTA not a near-term driver
items.quote: So I think it would be fair to say that to begin with, the focus is only domestic. We are not focusing on U.K. exports.

items.statement: Parliamentary Committee report on healthcare affordability noted; management believes policy will be rational and viable for efficient providers; no reassessment of expansion plans
items.quote: The Parliamentary Committee report does not put any thoughts or reassessment of expansion plans. My belief is that, eventually, you have to believe any sort of policy will be rational. We are efficient providers of healthcare.

items.statement: Shaheed Path and Thane projects: regulatory approvals in progress; after approval (~6 months), 30-36 months for delivery
items.quote: For both projects after the approval, which is another six months from now, after that they will take about 30 to 36 months for delivery.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for next 2-3 years
items.quote: on a consol basis, we should be looking at anything between 22% to 24% EBITDA margin is what I would really guide at

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 24-26%
items.quote: on a standalone, we should be looking at anything between 24% to 26% on a standalone basis

items.statement: Capex for standalone business guided at INR70-80 crores for FY27, mainly maintenance and repurposing
items.quote: in the range of INR70 crores to INR80 crores may be the number that I would look at from a capex point of view, for now

items.statement: No significant capex required for existing Anupam platform; major capex cycle completed
items.quote: we have now completed the major capex cycle that we had undertaken over the last few years. All our major planned projects have been commissioned and are operational. And therefore, we do not foresee a significant capex requirement for the existing Anupam platform in near term

items.statement: Cumulative signed LOIs and contracts represent ~INR18,000 crores potential business over respective tenures
items.quote: our cumulative signed LOI and contracts highlighted in the presentation represents roughly INR18,000 crores of potential business over their respective tenures

items.statement: Jayhawk contributed 20-22% of Q1 revenue with 19-20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Jayhawk has been contributing around about 20% to 22% of our revenue for this quarter, and the margins have been very robust at around about 19 to 20 percentage points

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin stable at 26% in Q1 FY27 despite higher performance materials share
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA margins for the quarter remained healthy at 26%, broadly stable on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Polymer business targeted at 20-25% of standalone revenue and 30-35% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: on a standalone, we should be able to get a polymer business to be in the range of 20% to 25%. And on a consolidated basis, it should be in the range of 30% to 35%

items.statement: Expect high-teens top-line growth for FY27, with potential to reach high-teens to 20% if current momentum sustains
items.quote: I think if the business continues to grow the way that it is doing now, I think it is a good possibility that we should be looking at between high-teens to 20% as overall revenue. Yes.

items.statement: Peak annual revenue of new business ex-ADS stood at INR18.5 billion as of June 2026
items.quote: Therefore, as of June 2026, our peak annual revenue of our new business ex of ADS stood at INR18.5 billion.

items.statement: New 80,000 sq ft hangar for aero and SEM business to be commissioned in a month or two; build-to-suit facility adding 100,000 sq ft expected ready in 10 months
items.quote: We are also working on a build-to-suit facility not far from our existing place, which we hope to conclude discussions in August and have that facility ready in about 10 months' time, and that would add a further 100,000 square foot to our manufacturing space.

items.statement: Capex projects on ADS and auto sides to come on stream beginning Q3 FY27 and complete within a year
items.quote: The project that I mentioned on both ADS and auto sites will come on stream beginning of Q3 FY27 onwards, and we will get it completed within a year from now.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded ~200 bps YoY to 19.2% in Q1 FY27; management targets inching towards 19% for full year, with 20-20-20 aspirational goal
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanding by around 200 basis points to 19.2% compared with 17.2% in the same quarter previous year.

items.statement: ADS and exports businesses target 25-30% EBITDA margins, trending towards high-20s as utilization improves
items.quote: I would say that as we improve our capacity utilization, the numbers would be more towards higher north of high-20s. I don't want to put a figure into it, but then definitely this would be between 25% and 30% margins.

items.statement: Material cost increase seen primarily in aluminum and consumables; steel inflation limited; pass-through negotiations with customers in process but not yet materialized
items.quote: We see limited inflation, and we are engaging with our customers for the pass-through, which is currently in process, not yet translated. And that's where we stand right now.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility in domestic 2W and PV for at least next 1.5 quarters; export traction in PV, premium 2W, off-road; energy segment deliveries to North America customer from Q3
items.quote: I see a very strong demand visibility both in two-wheeler and passenger vehicle for at least next one and a half quarters, definitely.

items.quote: Probably by end of decade is what we said that we will have an opportunity to look at overall revenue of about INR8,000 crore to INR 9,000 crore. That is what is the plan with which we are working on.

items.quote: Historically, we have seen that the Asia Pacific region has had a CAGR growth of 7% to 8%. And there are reports which indicate that up to 2025, this will continue to grow at a reasonable pace. I believe by 2035, the market is expected to touch a size of $1.4 billion.

items.statement: Launched HiCel SMCC Nutra for nutraceutical formulations; advancing Croscarmellose Sodium (CCS) facility (1,800 MTPA) at Dahej SEZ
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched HiCel SMCC Nutra, a unique combination of microcrystalline cellulose and magnesium aluminometasilicate, purpose-built to address flowability, compressibility and processing challenges in the nutraceutical formulations.

items.statement: Planning preferential equity issue and/or bank term loans to fund FY27-FY28 capex; company currently debt-free
items.quote: Yes. That's what now, we can borrow and as well as we can raise some preferential equity that we'll come up with an announcement once that is finalized.

items.statement: API business targeting >INR100-110 crore annual revenue; new molecules Sparsentan, Bempedoic Acid, Zestrapin driving growth
items.quote: In API we have new molecules like Sparsentan and Bempedoic Acid is there and which gives higher margins and this quarter we achieved around INR21 crores of top line and next quarter, coming quarters, quarter-on-quarter there will be improvement and we are expected to achieve more than INR100 crores to INR110 crores or

items.quote: This quarter, utilization at overall for all the company level, 76.8% is there; at Dahej unit 76.5%; and Jhagadia, it is 77.16%. And on an average, 76.8% is there. In next quarter, it will go up.

items.statement: Receivable days currently 93-94; target to reduce to 90 days by year-end and 75-80 days eventually
items.quote: Right now, it is around 90 plus is there, 93, 94 days.

items.statement: Consumables business long-term revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% CAGR
items.quote: There's no seasonality. And the 15% revenue guidance for consumable business on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to remain around 15% for full year
items.quote: Yes, we expect it to be in that range of 15% on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Molycop EBITDA margin expected to be relatively flat in upcoming quarters
items.quote: So, the margin should be relatively flat in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Tega capex approximately USD40 million including Chile plant; Molycop capex USD28 million for 10-month period
items.quote: So, Tega will be, excluding Molycop, will be USD40 million approximately, including Chile.

items.statement: Molycop normalized annual capex in low USD30 million range
items.quote: I'd say the ongoing normalized capital for Molycop would be in the low USD30 million.

items.statement: Healthy order book of INR12.3 billion with INR9.6 billion executable within one year
items.quote: The total order book for the Consumable and Equipment segment stands at INR12.3 billion, out of which executable within one year is approximately INR9.6 million.

items.statement: Tega consumables EBITDA margin expanded to 24.1% from 20.9% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 24.1% compared with 20.9% in the prior year, representing a significant improvement of 320 basis points.

items.statement: Tega legacy business gross margins maintained at ~62% despite raw material volatility
items.quote: Excluding Molycop, the group maintained healthy gross margins of approximately 62% compared with 59% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Freight cost increases passed through to customers with ~1 quarter lag
items.quote: We have seen container prices go up in different geographies that we ship to, but we have that in our contracts with customers that we are able to pass through those freight increases.

items.statement: Molycop contracts 85% tied to steel indices protecting gross margin per ton
items.quote: Around 85% of our contracts have a movement based on steel indexes. So, when steel goes up, revenue goes up and similar to if it moves downward, our revenue will move downward.

items.statement: Global copper demand projected to grow 4.8% CAGR, gold 2.2% CAGR through FY30
items.quote: According to UNCTAD, global copper demand is expected to increase by more than 40% by the year 2040.

items.statement: Cross-sell revenue ramp-up expected from Q3-Q4 FY27 as teams integrate
items.quote: We expect the revenue ramp up to actually happen from Q3 to Q4 onwards of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Chile plant soft commissioning January 2027, commercial production March 2027 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: We're looking at a soft commissioning around January 2027 with commercial production starting March.

items.statement: Group net debt reduced by INR32.18 billion to INR63.66 billion; further deleveraging expected
items.quote: Total net debt declined by roughly INR32.18 billion or USD340 million during the quarter ending at INR63.66 billion or USD672.5 million as of June 30.

items.statement: EEI business guided at ~20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for FY27; management expects to beat guidance but will not raise it
items.quote: The guidelines have been anywhere between 20% to 25% top line -- around 20% top line growth and EBITDA of 20% to 22% we have said.

items.statement: Current transformer capacity being doubled from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 units per day; additional machinery ordered
items.quote: Our capacity per day was around 5,000 to 6,000 low-voltage current transformers we were making. So as we speak, we are enhancing it to 8,000 to 10,000 now.

items.quote: In Q1, we further strengthened the solar inverter portfolio with the addition of the next generation of 3-phase iNEO inverter models up to 12 kilowatts in addition to the single-phase iUNO up to 5 kilowatts.

items.statement: Lumel Alucast has strong RFQ pipeline at advanced commercial/qualification stages; conversion to production programs expected to fill capacity progressively
items.quote: The RFQs with the number of new projects that we floated in the last year is now progressing through advanced commercial negotiations, qualifications and customer approval stages.

items.statement: Europe industrial environment relatively subdued; Lumel S.A. growth driven by multiple revenue streams (radiation gates, medium-voltage, grid upgradation) not dependent on macro
items.quote: While industrial activities in Europe remained relatively moderate, we continue to see encouraging opportunities across the U.S., Middle East, Southeast Asia and Africa.

items.statement: Acquisition ticket size typically INR50-200 cr; evaluating 4-5 opportunities in India, US, Europe; strong due diligence process; no specific timeline
items.quote: Typically, we look for acquisitions in the range of anywhere between INR50 crores to, say, about INR150 crores to INR200 crores based on how strategically it fits with our business.

items.statement: Net cash and equivalents INR1,606 million as of June 30, 2026; company remains net debt-free
items.quote: On the consolidated level, we remain net debt-free with a strong balance sheet. Net cash and cash equivalents as on 30th of June 2026 stands at INR1,606 million.

items.statement: India multi-channel revenue growth expected to remain elevated in subsequent quarters of FY27 due to structural initiatives

items.statement: International business aims to become EBITDA neutral as soon as possible, with losses reducing from 10% to 7% of revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Objective is to solve for becoming an EBITDA neutral business as soon as possible and then GlobalBees continue to demonstrate a improvement in adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: GlobalBees revenue growth expected to bounce back starting Q3 FY27 after temporary warehouse transition impact in Q1-Q2
items.quote: This is a temporary and planned transition that should be complete in Q2 and therefore we expect the growth to bounce back starting Q3.

items.statement: Plan to add 90-100 net new offline stores in FY27, with accelerated expansion in FY28
items.quote: So we'll be able to add that for this fiscal year. And so, that's the answer to the store expansion question. Obviously, FY28 will be even better because we were waiting for this transition to happen that we just spoke about.

items.statement: RocketBees expanded to 72 cities covering over 50% of online shipments, with 20% improvement in delivery turnaround time

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24% in Q1 FY27 vs 4.98% YoY; India multi-channel EBITDA margin down 290 bps YoY due to gross margin pressure
items.quote: Overall revenue from operations grew by 13% to 2,106 crores. And consolidated EBITDA- adjusted EBITDA grew to 4.24% versus 4.98%. At 289.3 crores, consolidated gross margin likewise to 36.5 from 38.5.

And in loss terms, as compared to revenue, we had an improvement by 320 bps from 10% to 7%.

items.statement: Passing on crude-linked raw material cost increases and rupee depreciation impact to customers in manufacturing business, expected full pass-through by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: On the loss of margins in manufacturing business, we have started passing the increase in crude linked raw material prices in manufacturing business to our customers and expect to fully recover it by the end of this quarter.

items.statement: Offline business shifted from width to depth product assortment strategy, driving 15% GMV growth in Q1 FY27 with improved footfalls and conversions
items.quote: Third initiative that we have been speaking about, it's in full flow now. We had talked about that we will realign our product portfolio from a width to a depth strategy has really fully scaled out. The impact of this was visible, even in last quarter, and it continues in this quarter. It has held us to drive footfalls

items.statement: Management confident of achieving revenue of around INR500+ crores in FY27 and believes current growth pace can be sustained through the year.
items.quote: Based on the momentum we are seeing across our businesses and the pipeline currently in place, we are confident of achieving revenue of around INR500 plus crores in FY27.

items.statement: Management expects quarter-on-quarter revenue to remain relatively flat due to seasonality, with Q2 heavier but corporate travel dipping in festival months.
items.quote: On and all we feel that quarter-on-quarter in our line of business, there will not going to be a substantial growth.

items.quote: Another is the Punjab Yatra program, valued at around INR92 crores and covering approximately 1.85 lakh yatris.

items.statement: Corporate travel vertical launched in April, onboarded 100+ corporate clients, contributing 10-15% of revenue; recurring annual/multi-year relationships.
items.quote: We launched this vertical in April and have already onboarded more than 100 corporate clients.

items.quote: About INR100 crores came from the MICE business and about 10%, 15% came from the corporate business and similarly, about 15% came from the Punjab Yatra.

items.quote: One of the biggest milestones is that we would be eligible to come onto main board in next 12 months.

items.quote: The demand is, as I said, we just exhibited from the exhibition and we've come and we have a huge demand in export as well as in local.

items.quote: The reason for being negative cash flow is like, we utilize all the funds and we keep the stock readily. We don't deal on order-to-order basis.

items.statement: FY27 is a ramp-up year with no revenue or margin guidance; meaningful revenue from new verticals expected from FY28
items.quote: FY '27 we don't want to guide, it's purely a ramp-up year where we are completely focused on commercializing each of the verticals and we'll give a better guidance, we want to be more accurate with our guidance, so as the year passes, we'll give a more stronger guidance towards the end of the calendar year for the next

items.quote: On consolidated basis, gross profit stood at INR16.5 crores with a gross margin of 16.7%, while EBITDA stood at INR3.3 crores with an EBITDA margin of 3.3%.

items.statement: New products are margin-accretive vs existing portfolio; operating leverage to support margins as utilization improves
items.quote: as we develop new products, so how we're looking at it is, each new product that's coming in, we want it to be like more margin accretive than our existing products.

items.statement: Demand back to normal levels; Western Hemisphere (US, LatAm) ramping up; export order flow strong for mint and new products
items.quote: We effectively are seeing a situation where the demand from the Western Hemisphere, which is largely U.S. and Latin America, is ramping up.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary approved to expand distribution reach in Latin America for essential oils, aromatic and specialty chemicals
items.quote: The company has approved the incorporation of a Brazil subsidiary, representing another step towards expanding our distribution reach in Latin America and creating a dedicated platform for our essential oils, aromatic chemicals, and specialty chemicals.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.5% in Q1 FY27, up 110bps YoY and 80bps QoQ; driven by premium mix, calibrated price hikes, operating leverage

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken across selected categories absorbed input cost inflation without impacting demand; further hikes only if input costs require
items.quote: On the price side, we have already taken a calibrated increase, and which has absorbed well in the market, and further action would only follow if input costs require, but however the cost and the sourcing efficiency will always be the first preference.

items.statement: Broad-based double-digit growth across all categories in Q1; TV and washing machines expected to drive H2 growth; ACs and refrigerators to benefit from premiumization and replacement demand
items.quote: We see demand remaining very healthy across both Home Appliances and Home Entertainment in this financial year. What gives us the confidence that Q1 has already demonstrated that we can deliver a very strong growth even challenging external environment.

items.quote: In information display panels, our LED signages recorded its highest ever quarterly sale in the Q1. And with continuous inflow of government and corporate orders, we have also achieved 36% market share in this business.

items.statement: Government imposed quantitative restrictions on compressor imports (60% reciprocating, 70% rotary); LG benefits from local compressor capacity (1mn at Greater Noida, +2mn at Sri City)
items.quote: In this year, 8th of May, the Government of India, they introduced quantitative restriction on the import of compressors. items.statement: No external borrowing needed; Sri City INR5,000cr investment funded from internal accruals; cash balance INR57.07bn as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Preserving our internal accruals to fund this investment entirely without any external debt is a conscious and deliberate decision that we believe is in the best long-term interest of our shareholders.

items.statement: Localization rate 55.2% in FY26; targeting 65% over next 3-4 years; Sri City plant to accelerate localization and act as export hub
items.quote: Our localization rates for the last full year was at 55.2%. And we are continuing focus on further improving this in current year as well. items.statement: Data center cooling seen as long-term B2B opportunity; mid-scale segment already revenue-generating; hyper-scale at preliminary evaluation stage; not a key FY27 driver
items.quote: From a materiality standpoint, this is not a key driver for us in FY27 outlook, but yes, it aligns well with our long-term B2B growth strategy.

items.statement: Dividend payout deferred to fund Sri City capex; management commits to review dividend plans as investment progresses and cash generation strengthens
items.quote: We would like to assure our shareholders that this is not a permanent position. As our Sri City investment progresses in a phased manner and our cash generation strengthens further through revenue growth and margin improvement, we definitely plan to review our dividend plans.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR840 crore (granite INR720 crore, quartz INR100-120 crore) vs FY26 INR645 crore
items.quote: FY27 we will be close to -- we are estimating around INR840 crores against past year's number of INR645 crores.

items.statement: Granite EBITDA margin expected in same range as prior years (50-100 bps variance) unless diesel price impact
items.quote: Granite-wise, we will be achieving whatever we have recorded in the last few years. It will be more or less in the same lines. Except unless we have diesel price impact. We will be we will be like maybe a 50 bps to 100 bps kind of a range, we will be in the same lines as last years.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 2 capex ~INR125 crore split over FY27 and FY28; INR60-70 crore outflow in Q2-Q3 FY27
items.quote: Capex on quartz would be approximately INR125 crores.

items.statement: Sri Lanka project plant build capex ~INR120 crore
items.quote: Sri Lankan project for plant building it's around INR120 crores.

items.quote: Demand is good, you can see from the numbers we have 35% topline growth. I think if you remove the quartz part, we are still above 30. So I think the demand-wise is good, the pricing-wise we have had a better realization.

items.statement: Quartz sales mix: 65% engineered stone, 35% solar
items.quote: Around 60% to 65% engineered stone, balance solar. I think 65-35 is a reasonable assumption.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin FY27 ~26-27%; FY28 expected ~29-30% as quartz scales
items.quote: EBITDA would be close to 30%, little above 30%. And overall blended EBITDA might be around 29%, 30%.

items.quote: I think last year it was 35% of the overall year revenue. So that is also historically constant for us. So this year also I think it will be not be any different.

items.statement: Diesel cost volatility key risk; electrification of fleet and solar back-integration underway to reduce exposure
items.quote: The biggest lever in this is the volume growth, right revenue growth. So if if revenue growth is able to absorb most of the other costs, fixed costs and I think that revenue growth we will be able to meet, we feel as of now.

items.statement: MoU signed with Indonesia's PERMINAS for rare earths (ionic clays, heavy & light); JV formation expected this quarter; first production in 12-15 months post-JV

items.statement: Sri Lanka policy finalized; license expected this quarter; ground breaking ~October; plant build 12-15 months; revenue from FY29
items.quote: I think we will can start internally timelines we can start breaking the ground somewhere in October. So I think from that point of time, we should look at 12 to 15 months for the plant build-out and start operations.

items.statement: Kerala JV stalled awaiting new government MD appointment; progress expected next quarter

items.statement: Intent to keep operating costs flat in USD terms over coming couple of years; only INR cost changes from currency translation

items.statement: Gross profit per unit (yield) at current levels considered sustainable; incremental volume growth directly multiplies gross profit; EBITDA margin % not relevant due to freight pass-through
items.quote: In terms of the gross profit per unit of volume, we believe that the current levels can be sustained. So any incremental growth that you would see in volumes would be a direct multiplier on the gross profit.

items.statement: Sequential volume improvement across trade lanes: LCL and air up ~5% QoQ, FCL up ~1% QoQ; half of growth from market, half from outperformance
items.quote: As an outcome of that, we have seen incremental volumes in both LCL and air of the magnitude of about 5%, while on the FCL, we have seen a quarter-on-quarter growth rate of about 1%.
